75: # ## 2. Model comparison (held-out 12,800 sample customers)
76: #
77: # Two non-deep-learning baselines (logistic regression, gradient boosting), a PyTorch MLP
78: # averaged over three seeds, and two blended ensembles. PR-AUC is the primary metric because
79: # only 14.6% of sampled customers purchase.
80: 
81: 
82: display(comp.set_index("model")[["pr_auc", "roc_auc", "f1", "precision", "recall",
83:                                  "threshold", "brier"]].round(4))
84: 
85: 
86: # ### Interpretation
87: #
88: # - The blended **MLP + HGB** ensemble has the best PR-AUC and F1, so it is selected.
89: # - The MLP alone has the best F1 at its own threshold and is close on PR-AUC; blending with
90: #   gradient boosting improves ranking stability.
91: # - The dummy prior (PR-AUC 0.146) shows the lift from behavioural features.
92: 
93: 
94: fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4.6))
95: colors = plt.cm.tab10(np.linspace(0, 1, 10))
96: model_cols = [c for c in val.columns if c not in ("customer_id", "target")]
97: for i, name in enumerate(model_cols):
98:     fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(val["target"], val[name])
99:     axes[0].plot(fpr, tpr, lw=1.6, color=colors[i],
100:                  label=f"{name} ({roc_auc_score(val['target'], val[name]):.4f})")
101:     prec, rec, _ = precision_recall_curve(val["target"], val[name])
102:     axes[1].plot(rec, prec, lw=1.6, color=colors[i],
103:                  label=f"{name} ({average_precision_score(val['target'], val[name]):.4f})")
104: axes[0].plot([0, 1], [0, 1], "--", color="grey", lw=1)
105: axes[0].set(title="ROC curves (validation)", xlabel="False positive rate",
106:             ylabel="True positive rate")
107: axes[1].axhline(val["target"].mean(), ls="--", color="grey", lw=1, label="prior")
108: axes[1].set(title="Precision-recall curves (validation)", xlabel="Recall",
109:             ylabel="Precision")
110: for ax in axes:
111:     ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
112:     ax.legend(fontsize=6.5, loc="best")
113: plt.tight_layout()
114: plt.show()
115: 
116: 
117: prob = val[SEL].to_numpy()
118: y = val["target"].to_numpy()
119: pred = (prob >= THR).astype(int)
120: tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y, pred, labels=[0, 1]).ravel()
121: out = pd.DataFrame({
122:     "metric": ["precision", "recall", "f1", "accuracy", "flagged", "tp", "fp", "fn", "tn"],
123:     "value": [tp / max(tp + fp, 1), tp / max(tp + fn, 1),
124:               2 * tp / max(2 * tp + fp + fn, 1), (tp + tn) / len(y), pred.mean(),
125:               tp, fp, fn, tn],
126: })
127: display(out.round(4))
128: 
129: fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4, 3.2))
130: ConfusionMatrixDisplay(np.array([[tn, fp], [fn, tp]]),
131:                        display_labels=["No buy", "Buy"]).plot(
132:     ax=ax, colorbar=False, cmap="Blues")
133: ax.set_title(f"{SEL} @ {THR:.3f}")
134: plt.show()
135: 
136: 
137: # ## 3. Deep-learning model
138: #
139: # A 256-128-64 MLP with batch norm, dropout, class-weighted BCE, AdamW and early stopping,
140: # averaged over three seeds. The chart shows validation PR-AUC per epoch; early stopping
141: # restored each seed's best epoch.
142: 
143: 
144: log = pd.read_csv(REPORTS / "mlp_training_log.csv")
145: pivot = log.pivot_table(index="epoch", columns="seed", values="val_ap")
146: pivot.plot(figsize=(9, 4), marker="o", ms=2.5)
147: plt.title("MLP validation PR-AUC by epoch and seed")
148: plt.xlabel("epoch")
149: plt.ylabel("validation PR-AUC")
150: plt.grid(alpha=0.25)
151: plt.legend(title="seed")
152: plt.show()
153: 
154: 
155: # ## 4. Feature importance
156: #
157: # Permutation importance on the gradient-boosting model (drop in validation PR-AUC when a
158: # transformed feature is shuffled). Behavioural recency and frequency dominate, which matches
159: # the retention domain.
160: 
161: 
162: imp = pd.read_csv(REPORTS / "feature_importance_hgb.csv").head(18).iloc[::-1]
163: imp.plot.barh(x="feature", y="importance", figsize=(9, 5.2), legend=False, color="#2c6fbb")
164: plt.title("Top permutation importances (HGB, validation PR-AUC drop)")
165: plt.xlabel("drop in PR-AUC")
166: plt.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.25)
167: plt.tight_layout()
168: plt.show()
169: 
170: 
171: # ## 5. Segment and fairness analysis
172: #
173: # Because the data is a sample, analysis is done at segment level. The tier snapshot shows how
174: # a large low-propensity group (Bronze) differs from a small high-propensity group (Platinum).
175: # The multi-group table then intersects conditions - for example Bronze AND active AND high
176: # session volume, or email opt-in AND high sessions - so we can see which combinations carry
177: # the expected buyers.
178: 
179: 
180: test = pd.read_pickle(FEAT / "test_features.pkl")
181: probs = pd.read_csv(REPORTS / "test_probabilities.csv")
182: tv = probs[["customer_id", "selected_probability"]].merge(
183:     test[["customer_id", "cust_country", "cust_tier", "pref_email_opt", "pref_dnc",
184:           "sup_open_n", "sup_recent_complaint", "sup_n", "cust_loyalty", "tenure_days",
185:           "sess_n_180d", "sess_days_since_last", "txn_spend_180d", "txn_days_since_last"]],
186:     on="customer_id")
187: tv["flagged"] = tv["selected_probability"] >= THR
188: tv["recency_band"] = np.select(
189:     [tv["sess_days_since_last"].isna(), tv["sess_days_since_last"] <= 7,
190:      tv["sess_days_since_last"] <= 30, tv["sess_days_since_last"] <= 90],
191:     ["No session", "Active <=7d", "Warm 8-30d", "Cooling 31-90d"], default="Dormant >90d")
192: tv["loyalty_band"] = pd.qcut(tv["cust_loyalty"].rank(method="first"), 4,
193:                              labels=["Q1 low", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4 high"])
194: tv["session_band"] = pd.qcut(tv["sess_n_180d"].rank(method="first"), 4,
195:                              labels=["Q1 low", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4 high"])
196: tv["spend_band"] = pd.qcut(tv["txn_spend_180d"].rank(method="first"), 4,
197:                            labels=["Q1 low", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4 high"])
198: 
199: 
200: def summarize(frame, by):
201:     g = frame.groupby(by, observed=True).agg(
202:         customers=("selected_probability", "size"),
203:         mean_propensity=("selected_probability", "mean"),
204:         expected_buyers=("selected_probability", "sum"),
205:         flag_rate=("selected_probability", lambda s: (s >= THR).mean()))
206:     g["share_expected"] = g["expected_buyers"] / frame["selected_probability"].sum()
207:     return g.sort_values("expected_buyers", ascending=False)
208: 
209: 
210: print("Tier snapshot (test sample)")
211: display(summarize(tv, "cust_tier").round(3))
212: print("Country snapshot (test sample)")
213: display(summarize(tv, "cust_country").round(3))
214: 
215: segments = {
216:     "Bronze + active + high sessions": (tv["cust_tier"] == "Bronze") & (tv["recency_band"] == "Active <=7d") & (tv["session_band"] == "Q4 high"),
217:     "Email opt-in + high sessions": (tv["pref_email_opt"] == 1) & (tv["session_band"] == "Q4 high"),
218:     "Bronze + email opt-in": (tv["cust_tier"] == "Bronze") & (tv["pref_email_opt"] == 1),
219:     "High loyalty + cooling": (tv["loyalty_band"] == "Q4 high") & (tv["recency_band"] == "Cooling 31-90d"),
220:     "Gold/Silver + recent complaint": tv["cust_tier"].isin(["Gold", "Silver"]) & (tv["sup_recent_complaint"] == 1),
221:     "High spend + dormant": (tv["spend_band"] == "Q4 high") & (tv["recency_band"] == "Dormant >90d"),
222:     "Platinum + dormant": (tv["cust_tier"] == "Platinum") & (tv["recency_band"] == "Dormant >90d"),
223:     "Open complaint (all tiers)": tv["sup_open_n"].fillna(0) > 0,
224:     "DNC customers": tv["pref_dnc"] == 1,
225: }
226: rows = []
227: total = tv["selected_probability"].sum()
228: for name, mask in segments.items():
229:     s = tv.loc[mask, "selected_probability"]
230:     rows.append({"segment": name, "customers": len(s), "mean_propensity": s.mean(),
231:                  "expected_buyers": s.sum(), "share_expected": s.sum() / total,
232:                  "flag_rate": (s >= THR).mean() if len(s) else np.nan})
233: print("\nMulti-group intersections (test sample)")
234: display(pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("expected_buyers", ascending=False).round(3))
235: 
236: pivot = tv.pivot_table(index="cust_tier", columns="recency_band",
237:                        values="selected_probability", aggfunc="mean")
238: pivot = pivot.reindex(columns=[c for c in ["Active <=7d", "Warm 8-30d", "Cooling 31-90d",
239:                                           "Dormant >90d", "No session"] if c in pivot.columns])
240: fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.4))
241: im = ax.imshow(pivot.to_numpy(dtype=float), cmap="Blues", aspect="auto")
242: ax.set_xticks(range(len(pivot.columns)))
243: ax.set_xticklabels(pivot.columns, rotation=20, ha="right")
244: ax.set_yticks(range(len(pivot.index)))
245: ax.set_yticklabels(pivot.index)
246: for i in range(pivot.shape[0]):
247:     for j in range(pivot.shape[1]):
248:         v = pivot.iloc[i, j]
249:         if pd.notna(v):
250:             ax.text(j, i, f"{v:.2f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9)
251: ax.set_title("Mean propensity by tier x session recency")
252: plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.03)
253: plt.tight_layout()
254: plt.show()
255: 
256: for key in ["cust_country", "cust_tier"]:
257:     table = (tv.groupby(key).agg(customers=("flagged", "size"),
258:                                  flagged=("flagged", "sum"))
259:              .assign(selection_rate=lambda d: d["flagged"] / d["customers"])
260:              .sort_values("selection_rate", ascending=False))
261:     print(f"\nSelection rate by {key}")
262:     display(table.round(3))
263: print("\nDNC customers excluded from outreach by policy:", int((tv["pref_dnc"] == 1).sum()))
264: print("Customers with open complaints:", int((tv["sup_open_n"].fillna(0) > 0).sum()))
265: 
266: 
267: # ## 6. First test submission
268: #
269: # The submission flags the top-scoring rows of the test sample at the tuned threshold. The top
270: # decile carries most of the expected purchases, so outreach can be prioritised by segment.
271: 
272: 
273: fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3))
274: ax.hist(probs["selected_probability"], bins=40, color="#2c6fbb", alpha=0.85)
275: ax.axvline(THR, color="#c0392b", ls="--", label=f"threshold {THR:.2f}")
276: ax.set(xlabel="predicted probability", ylabel="sample customers",
277:        title="Test propensity distribution")
278: ax.legend()
279: ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
280: plt.show()
281: 
282: flagged = (probs["selected_probability"] >= THR).astype(int)
283: top_decile = probs["selected_probability"] >= probs["selected_probability"].quantile(0.9)
284: share = (probs.loc[top_decile, "selected_probability"].sum()
285:          / probs["selected_probability"].sum())
286: print(f"flagged {flagged.sum():,} of {len(flagged):,} ({flagged.mean():.1%})")
287: print(f"top-decile share of expected purchases: {share:.1%}")
288: print(probs["selected_probability"].describe().round(4))
289: 
290: 
291: # ## 7. Agentic win-back preview (segment policy layer)
292: #
293: # The agent will call this policy tool. It filters rows by consent/DNC, open complaints and
294: # recent contact, assigns an offer by tier and caps spend by the weekly per-country budget.
295: # The output is aggregated to segments so no individual customer record is exposed.
296: 
297: 
298: offers = pd.read_csv(DATA / "offer_catalogue.csv")
299: budget = pd.read_csv(DATA / "retention_budget_2024Q4.csv")
300: plan_src = tv.merge(test[["customer_id", "pref_channel", "ret_days_since_last"]],
301:                     on="customer_id").drop(columns=["customer_id"])
302: cand = plan_src[(plan_src["selected_probability"] >= THR)
303:                 & (plan_src["pref_dnc"] == 0)
304:                 & (plan_src["sup_open_n"].fillna(0) == 0)].copy()
305: cand = cand[cand["ret_days_since_last"].isna() | (cand["ret_days_since_last"] >= 14)].copy()
306: 
307: 
308: def tier_offer(r):
309:     if r["sup_recent_complaint"] == 1:
310:         return "OFF-SRC"
311:     return {"Platinum": "OFF-V20", "Gold": "OFF-V15",
312:             "Silver": "OFF-V15"}.get(r["cust_tier"], "OFF-FS")
313: 
314: 
315: cand["offer"] = cand.apply(tier_offer, axis=1)
316: AOV = 80.0
317: 
318: 
319: def cost(code):
320:     rec = offers.loc[offers["offer_code"] == code].iloc[0]
321:     return rec["value"] * AOV if rec["offer_type"] == "Voucher" else rec["value"]
322: 
323: 
324: cand["cost"] = cand["offer"].map(cost)
325: week = budget["week_start"].min()
326: caps = budget[budget["week_start"] == week].set_index("country")["retention_budget_usd"]
327: 
328: pick = []
329: for country, g in cand.sort_values("selected_probability", ascending=False).groupby("cust_country"):
330:     spent = 0.0
331:     for _, r in g.iterrows():
332:         if spent + r["cost"] > caps.get(country, 0):
333:             break
334:         pick.append(r)
335:         spent += r["cost"]
336: plan = pd.DataFrame(pick).sort_values("selected_probability", ascending=False)
337: print(f"week {week}: {len(cand):,} eligible -> {len(plan):,} contacts, "
338:       f"expected buyers {plan['selected_probability'].sum():.0f}, "
339:       f"spend ${plan['cost'].sum():,.0f}")
340: 
341: plan_agg = (plan.groupby(["cust_country", "cust_tier", "offer", "pref_channel"])
342:             .agg(contacts=("selected_probability", "size"),
343:                  expected_buyers=("selected_probability", "sum"),
344:                  estimated_spend=("cost", "sum"))
345:             .reset_index().sort_values("expected_buyers", ascending=False))
346: print("\nSegment-level plan (no customer IDs)")
347: display(plan_agg.round({"expected_buyers": 1, "estimated_spend": 2}).head(20))
348: 
349: print("\nOffer mix by tier")
350: display(plan.groupby(["cust_tier", "offer"])
351:         .agg(contacts=("selected_probability", "size"),
352:              expected_buyers=("selected_probability", "sum"),
353:              spend=("cost", "sum")).round({"expected_buyers": 1, "spend": 2}))
354: 
355: 
356: # ## 8. Limitations and next steps
357: #
358: # - **Sample, not census:** estimates describe segment tendencies; widen or reweight the
359: #   sample before making population claims.
360: # - **Causal vs predictive:** propensity is not uplift; run a randomised segment holdout
361: #   before scaling incentives.
362: # - **Temporal drift:** validate on the next 30-day window and monitor calibration monthly.
363: # - **Deep model:** seed ensembling helped slightly; try categorical embeddings next.
364: # - **Agent:** wrap the planner as a tool, add an LLM reasoner for offer explanation and a
365: #   human approval step for high-value segments.
366: # - **Deliverables:** this notebook, `reports/Week8_model_report.md`, `dashboard/app.py`

# # ShopSphere - Week 8 Model Checkpoint
#
# **IT2226 AI Innovation & Deep Learning**
#
# Predict whether a customer purchases in the 30 days after **2024-09-30** (October 2024).
#
# > **Sample framing.** The dataset is a sample of the customer base, not a full census.
# > Results describe segment-level tendencies and are not used to make decisions about
# > individual customers. No customer IDs appear in this notebook.
#
# | Item | Value |
# |---|---|
# | Modelling grain | one row per sampled customer |
# | Train / validation / test | 64,000 / 12,800 / 16,000 |
# | Target rate (train) | 14.6% |
# | Selected model | Ensemble (Deep MLP + Gradient Boosting) |


import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.metrics import (ConfusionMatrixDisplay, average_precision_score,
                             confusion_matrix, precision_recall_curve, roc_curve,
                             roc_auc_score)

pd.set_option("display.width", 160)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
plt.rcParams["figure.dpi"] = 110

BASE = Path.cwd()
if not (BASE / "artifacts").exists():
    BASE = BASE / "ShopSphere"
REPORTS = BASE / "artifacts" / "reports" / "fixed"
FEAT = BASE / "artifacts" / "features"
DATA = BASE / "data" / "clean"

metrics = json.loads((REPORTS / "metrics.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
comp = pd.read_csv(REPORTS / "model_comparison.csv").sort_values("pr_auc", ascending=False)
val = pd.read_csv(REPORTS / "validation_predictions.csv")
SEL, THR = metrics["selected_model"], metrics["selected_threshold"]

print(f"Selected model : {SEL}")
print(f"Threshold      : {THR:.3f}")
print(f"Split          : {metrics['split']}")
print(f"Test positives : {metrics['submission_positives']:,} ({metrics['submission_positive_rate']:.1%})")


# ## 1. Data and leakage control
#
# All features are built from data on or before the 2024-09-30 cutoff. The 64,000 train and
# 16,000 test rows are disjoint samples, and the target is purchases in the following 30-day
# window, so there is no target leakage. Sixteen cleaned source tables feed 156 customer-level
# features (150 numeric, 6 categorical).


rows = []
for p in sorted(DATA.glob("*.csv")):
    if p.name == "sample_submission.csv":
        continue
    with open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as fh:
        rows.append({"table": p.stem, "rows": sum(1 for _ in fh) - 1})
inventory = pd.DataFrame(rows)
display(inventory)
print("total rows:", f"{inventory['rows'].sum():,}", "| tables:", len(inventory))


# ## 2. Model comparison (held-out 12,800 sample customers)
#
# Two non-deep-learning baselines (logistic regression, gradient boosting), a PyTorch MLP
# averaged over three seeds, and two blended ensembles. PR-AUC is the primary metric because
# only 14.6% of sampled customers purchase.


display(comp.set_index("model")[["pr_auc", "roc_auc", "f1", "precision", "recall",
                                 "threshold", "brier"]].round(4))


# ### Interpretation
#
# - The blended **MLP + HGB** ensemble has the best PR-AUC and F1, so it is selected.
# - The MLP alone has the best F1 at its own threshold and is close on PR-AUC; blending with
#   gradient boosting improves ranking stability.
# - The dummy prior (PR-AUC 0.146) shows the lift from behavioural features.


fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4.6))
colors = plt.cm.tab10(np.linspace(0, 1, 10))
model_cols = [c for c in val.columns if c not in ("customer_id", "target")]
for i, name in enumerate(model_cols):
    fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(val["target"], val[name])
    axes[0].plot(fpr, tpr, lw=1.6, color=colors[i],
                 label=f"{name} ({roc_auc_score(val['target'], val[name]):.4f})")
    prec, rec, _ = precision_recall_curve(val["target"], val[name])
    axes[1].plot(rec, prec, lw=1.6, color=colors[i],
                 label=f"{name} ({average_precision_score(val['target'], val[name]):.4f})")
axes[0].plot([0, 1], [0, 1], "--", color="grey", lw=1)
axes[0].set(title="ROC curves (validation)", xlabel="False positive rate",
            ylabel="True positive rate")
axes[1].axhline(val["target"].mean(), ls="--", color="grey", lw=1, label="prior")
axes[1].set(title="Precision-recall curves (validation)", xlabel="Recall",
            ylabel="Precision")
for ax in axes:
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
    ax.legend(fontsize=6.5, loc="best")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()


prob = val[SEL].to_numpy()
y = val["target"].to_numpy()
pred = (prob >= THR).astype(int)
tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y, pred, labels=[0, 1]).ravel()
out = pd.DataFrame({
    "metric": ["precision", "recall", "f1", "accuracy", "flagged", "tp", "fp", "fn", "tn"],
    "value": [tp / max(tp + fp, 1), tp / max(tp + fn, 1),
              2 * tp / max(2 * tp + fp + fn, 1), (tp + tn) / len(y), pred.mean(),
              tp, fp, fn, tn],
})
display(out.round(4))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4, 3.2))
ConfusionMatrixDisplay(np.array([[tn, fp], [fn, tp]]),
                       display_labels=["No buy", "Buy"]).plot(
    ax=ax, colorbar=False, cmap="Blues")
ax.set_title(f"{SEL} @ {THR:.3f}")
plt.show()


# ## 3. Deep-learning model
#
# A 256-128-64 MLP with batch norm, dropout, class-weighted BCE, AdamW and early stopping,
# averaged over three seeds. The chart shows validation PR-AUC per epoch; early stopping
# restored each seed's best epoch.


log = pd.read_csv(REPORTS / "mlp_training_log.csv")
pivot = log.pivot_table(index="epoch", columns="seed", values="val_ap")
pivot.plot(figsize=(9, 4), marker="o", ms=2.5)
plt.title("MLP validation PR-AUC by epoch and seed")
plt.xlabel("epoch")
plt.ylabel("validation PR-AUC")
plt.grid(alpha=0.25)
plt.legend(title="seed")
plt.show()


# ## 4. Feature importance
#
# Permutation importance on the gradient-boosting model (drop in validation PR-AUC when a
# transformed feature is shuffled). Behavioural recency and frequency dominate, which matches
# the retention domain.


imp = pd.read_csv(REPORTS / "feature_importance_hgb.csv").head(18).iloc[::-1]
imp.plot.barh(x="feature", y="importance", figsize=(9, 5.2), legend=False, color="#2c6fbb")
plt.title("Top permutation importances (HGB, validation PR-AUC drop)")
plt.xlabel("drop in PR-AUC")
plt.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()


# ## 5. Segment and fairness analysis
#
# Because the data is a sample, analysis is done at segment level. The tier snapshot shows how
# a large low-propensity group (Bronze) differs from a small high-propensity group (Platinum).
# The multi-group table then intersects conditions - for example Bronze AND active AND high
# session volume, or email opt-in AND high sessions - so we can see which combinations carry
# the expected buyers.


test = pd.read_pickle(FEAT / "test_features.pkl")
probs = pd.read_csv(REPORTS / "test_probabilities.csv")
tv = probs[["customer_id", "selected_probability"]].merge(
    test[["customer_id", "cust_country", "cust_tier", "pref_email_opt", "pref_dnc",
          "sup_open_n", "sup_recent_complaint", "sup_n", "cust_loyalty", "tenure_days",
          "sess_n_180d", "sess_days_since_last", "txn_spend_180d", "txn_days_since_last"]],
    on="customer_id")
tv["flagged"] = tv["selected_probability"] >= THR
tv["recency_band"] = np.select(
    [tv["sess_days_since_last"].isna(), tv["sess_days_since_last"] <= 7,
     tv["sess_days_since_last"] <= 30, tv["sess_days_since_last"] <= 90],
    ["No session", "Active <=7d", "Warm 8-30d", "Cooling 31-90d"], default="Dormant >90d")
tv["loyalty_band"] = pd.qcut(tv["cust_loyalty"].rank(method="first"), 4,
                             labels=["Q1 low", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4 high"])
tv["session_band"] = pd.qcut(tv["sess_n_180d"].rank(method="first"), 4,
                             labels=["Q1 low", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4 high"])
tv["spend_band"] = pd.qcut(tv["txn_spend_180d"].rank(method="first"), 4,
                           labels=["Q1 low", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4 high"])


def summarize(frame, by):
    g = frame.groupby(by, observed=True).agg(
        customers=("selected_probability", "size"),
        mean_propensity=("selected_probability", "mean"),
        expected_buyers=("selected_probability", "sum"),
        flag_rate=("selected_probability", lambda s: (s >= THR).mean()))
    g["share_expected"] = g["expected_buyers"] / frame["selected_probability"].sum()
    return g.sort_values("expected_buyers", ascending=False)


print("Tier snapshot (test sample)")
display(summarize(tv, "cust_tier").round(3))
print("Country snapshot (test sample)")
display(summarize(tv, "cust_country").round(3))

segments = {
    "Bronze + active + high sessions": (tv["cust_tier"] == "Bronze") & (tv["recency_band"] == "Active <=7d") & (tv["session_band"] == "Q4 high"),
    "Email opt-in + high sessions": (tv["pref_email_opt"] == 1) & (tv["session_band"] == "Q4 high"),
    "Bronze + email opt-in": (tv["cust_tier"] == "Bronze") & (tv["pref_email_opt"] == 1),
    "High loyalty + cooling": (tv["loyalty_band"] == "Q4 high") & (tv["recency_band"] == "Cooling 31-90d"),
    "Gold/Silver + recent complaint": tv["cust_tier"].isin(["Gold", "Silver"]) & (tv["sup_recent_complaint"] == 1),
    "High spend + dormant": (tv["spend_band"] == "Q4 high") & (tv["recency_band"] == "Dormant >90d"),
    "Platinum + dormant": (tv["cust_tier"] == "Platinum") & (tv["recency_band"] == "Dormant >90d"),
    "Open complaint (all tiers)": tv["sup_open_n"].fillna(0) > 0,
    "DNC customers": tv["pref_dnc"] == 1,
}
rows = []
total = tv["selected_probability"].sum()
for name, mask in segments.items():
    s = tv.loc[mask, "selected_probability"]
    rows.append({"segment": name, "customers": len(s), "mean_propensity": s.mean(),
                 "expected_buyers": s.sum(), "share_expected": s.sum() / total,
                 "flag_rate": (s >= THR).mean() if len(s) else np.nan})
print("\nMulti-group intersections (test sample)")
display(pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("expected_buyers", ascending=False).round(3))

pivot = tv.pivot_table(index="cust_tier", columns="recency_band",
                       values="selected_probability", aggfunc="mean")
pivot = pivot.reindex(columns=[c for c in ["Active <=7d", "Warm 8-30d", "Cooling 31-90d",
                                          "Dormant >90d", "No session"] if c in pivot.columns])
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.4))
im = ax.imshow(pivot.to_numpy(dtype=float), cmap="Blues", aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(pivot.columns)))
ax.set_xticklabels(pivot.columns, rotation=20, ha="right")
ax.set_yticks(range(len(pivot.index)))
ax.set_yticklabels(pivot.index)
for i in range(pivot.shape[0]):
    for j in range(pivot.shape[1]):
        v = pivot.iloc[i, j]
        if pd.notna(v):
            ax.text(j, i, f"{v:.2f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=9)
ax.set_title("Mean propensity by tier x session recency")
plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.03)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

for key in ["cust_country", "cust_tier"]:
    table = (tv.groupby(key).agg(customers=("flagged", "size"),
                                 flagged=("flagged", "sum"))
             .assign(selection_rate=lambda d: d["flagged"] / d["customers"])
             .sort_values("selection_rate", ascending=False))
    print(f"\nSelection rate by {key}")
    display(table.round(3))
print("\nDNC customers excluded from outreach by policy:", int((tv["pref_dnc"] == 1).sum()))
print("Customers with open complaints:", int((tv["sup_open_n"].fillna(0) > 0).sum()))


# ## 6. First test submission
#
# The submission flags the top-scoring rows of the test sample at the tuned threshold. The top
# decile carries most of the expected purchases, so outreach can be prioritised by segment.


fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 3))
ax.hist(probs["selected_probability"], bins=40, color="#2c6fbb", alpha=0.85)
ax.axvline(THR, color="#c0392b", ls="--", label=f"threshold {THR:.2f}")
ax.set(xlabel="predicted probability", ylabel="sample customers",
       title="Test propensity distribution")
ax.legend()
ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
plt.show()

flagged = (probs["selected_probability"] >= THR).astype(int)
top_decile = probs["selected_probability"] >= probs["selected_probability"].quantile(0.9)
share = (probs.loc[top_decile, "selected_probability"].sum()
         / probs["selected_probability"].sum())
print(f"flagged {flagged.sum():,} of {len(flagged):,} ({flagged.mean():.1%})")
print(f"top-decile share of expected purchases: {share:.1%}")
print(probs["selected_probability"].describe().round(4))


# ## 7. Agentic win-back preview (segment policy layer)
#
# The agent will call this policy tool. It filters rows by consent/DNC, open complaints and
# recent contact, assigns an offer by tier and caps spend by the weekly per-country budget.
# The output is aggregated to segments so no individual customer record is exposed.


offers = pd.read_csv(DATA / "offer_catalogue.csv")
budget = pd.read_csv(DATA / "retention_budget_2024Q4.csv")
plan_src = tv.merge(test[["customer_id", "pref_channel", "ret_days_since_last"]],
                    on="customer_id").drop(columns=["customer_id"])
cand = plan_src[(plan_src["selected_probability"] >= THR)
                & (plan_src["pref_dnc"] == 0)
                & (plan_src["sup_open_n"].fillna(0) == 0)].copy()
cand = cand[cand["ret_days_since_last"].isna() | (cand["ret_days_since_last"] >= 14)].copy()


def tier_offer(r):
    if r["sup_recent_complaint"] == 1:
        return "OFF-SRC"
    return {"Platinum": "OFF-V20", "Gold": "OFF-V15",
            "Silver": "OFF-V15"}.get(r["cust_tier"], "OFF-FS")


cand["offer"] = cand.apply(tier_offer, axis=1)
AOV = 80.0


def cost(code):
    rec = offers.loc[offers["offer_code"] == code].iloc[0]
    return rec["value"] * AOV if rec["offer_type"] == "Voucher" else rec["value"]


cand["cost"] = cand["offer"].map(cost)
week = budget["week_start"].min()
caps = budget[budget["week_start"] == week].set_index("country")["retention_budget_usd"]

pick = []
for country, g in cand.sort_values("selected_probability", ascending=False).groupby("cust_country"):
    spent = 0.0
    for _, r in g.iterrows():
        if spent + r["cost"] > caps.get(country, 0):
            break
        pick.append(r)
        spent += r["cost"]
plan = pd.DataFrame(pick).sort_values("selected_probability", ascending=False)
print(f"week {week}: {len(cand):,} eligible -> {len(plan):,} contacts, "
      f"expected buyers {plan['selected_probability'].sum():.0f}, "
      f"spend ${plan['cost'].sum():,.0f}")

plan_agg = (plan.groupby(["cust_country", "cust_tier", "offer", "pref_channel"])
            .agg(contacts=("selected_probability", "size"),
                 expected_buyers=("selected_probability", "sum"),
                 estimated_spend=("cost", "sum"))
            .reset_index().sort_values("expected_buyers", ascending=False))
print("\nSegment-level plan (no customer IDs)")
display(plan_agg.round({"expected_buyers": 1, "estimated_spend": 2}).head(20))

print("\nOffer mix by tier")
display(plan.groupby(["cust_tier", "offer"])
        .agg(contacts=("selected_probability", "size"),
             expected_buyers=("selected_probability", "sum"),
             spend=("cost", "sum")).round({"expected_buyers": 1, "spend": 2}))


# ## 8. Limitations and next steps
#
# - **Sample, not census:** estimates describe segment tendencies; widen or reweight the
#   sample before making population claims.
# - **Causal vs predictive:** propensity is not uplift; run a randomised segment holdout
#   before scaling incentives.
# - **Temporal drift:** validate on the next 30-day window and monitor calibration monthly.
# - **Deep model:** seed ensembling helped slightly; try categorical embeddings next.
# - **Agent:** wrap the planner as a tool, add an LLM reasoner for offer explanation and a
#   human approval step for high-value segments.
# - **Deliverables:** this notebook, `reports/Week8_model_report.md`, `dashboard/app.py`
#   (interactive segment viewer/tester) and `submission.csv`.

# ShopSphere - Week 8 Model Checkpoint

**IT2226 AI Innovation & Deep Learning**

Predict whether a customer purchases in the 30 days after **2024-09-30** (October 2024).

> **Sample framing.** The dataset is a sample of the customer base, not a full census.
> Results describe segment-level tendencies and are not used to make decisions about
> individual customers. No customer IDs appear in this notebook.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Modelling grain | one row per sampled customer |
| Train / validation / test | 64,000 / 12,800 / 16,000 |
| Target rate (train) | 14.6% |
| Selected model | Ensemble (Deep MLP + Gradient Boosting) |
--- 1 code ---
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.metrics import (ConfusionMatrixDisplay, average_precision_score,
                             confusion_matrix, precision_recall_curve, roc_curve,
                             roc_auc_score)

pd.set_option("display.width", 160)
pd.set_option("display.max_columns", 40)
plt.rcParams["figure.dpi"] = 110

BASE = Path.cwd()
if not (BASE / "artifacts").exists():
    BASE = BASE / "ShopSphere"
REPORTS = BASE / "artifacts" / "reports" / "fixed"
FEAT = BASE / "artifacts" / "features"
DATA = BASE / "data" / "clean"

metrics = json.loads((REPORTS / "metrics.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
comp = pd.read_csv(REPORTS / "model_comparison.csv").sort_values("pr_auc", ascending=False)
val = pd.read_csv(REPORTS / "validation_predictions.csv")
SEL, THR = metrics["selected_model"], metrics["selected_threshold"]

print(f"Selected model : {SEL}")
print(f"Threshold      : {THR:.3f}")
print(f"Split          : {metrics['split']}")
print(f"Test positives : {metrics['submission_positives']:,} ({metrics['submission_positive_rate']:.1%})")
--- 2 markdown ---
## 1. Data and leakage control

All features are built from data on or before the 2024-09-30 cutoff. The 64,000 train and
16,000 test rows are disjoint samples, and the target is purchases in the following 30-day
window, so there is no target leakage. Sixteen cleaned source tables feed 156 customer-level
features (150 numeric, 6 categorical).
--- 3 code ---
rows = []
for p in sorted(DATA.glob("*.csv")):
    if p.name == "sample_submission.csv":
        continue
    with open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as fh:
        rows.append({"table": p.stem, "rows": sum(1 for _ in fh) - 1})
inventory = pd.DataFrame(rows)
display(inventory)
print("total rows:", f"{inventory['rows'].sum():,}", "| tables:", len(inventory))
--- 4 markdown ---
## 2. Model comparison (held-out 12,800 sample customers)

Two non-deep-learning baselines (logistic regression, gradient boosting), a PyTorch MLP
averaged over three seeds, and two blended ensembles. PR-AUC is the primary metric because
only 14.6% of sampled customers purchase.
--- 5 code ---
display(comp.set_index("model")[["pr_auc", "roc_auc", "f1", "precision", "recall",
                                 "threshold", "brier"]].round(4))
--- 6 markdown ---
### Interpretation

- The blended **MLP + HGB** ensemble has the best PR-AUC and F1, so it is selected.
- The MLP alone has the best F1 at its own threshold and is close on PR-AUC; blending with
  gradient boosting improves ranking stability.
- The dummy prior (PR-AUC 0.146) shows the lift from behavioural features.
--- 7 code ---
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4.6))
colors = plt.cm.tab10(np.linspace(0, 1, 10))
model_cols = [c for c in val.columns if c not in ("customer_id", "target")]
for i, name in enumerate(model_cols):
    fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(val["target"], val[name])
    axes[0].plot(fpr, tpr, lw=1.6, color=colors[i],
                 label=f"{name} ({roc_auc_score(val['target'], val[name]):.4f})")
    prec, rec, _ = precision_recall_curve(val["target"], val[name])
    axes[1].plot(rec, prec, lw=1.6, color=colors[i],
                 label=f"{name} ({average_precision_score(val['target'], val[name]):.4f})")
axes[0].plot([0, 1], [0, 1], "--", color="grey", lw=1)
axes[0].set(title="ROC curves (validation)", xlabel="False positive rate",
            ylabel="True positive rate")
axes[1].axhline(val["target"].mean(), ls="--", color="grey", lw=1, label="prior")
axes[1].set(title="Precision-recall curves (validation)", xlabel="Recall",
            ylabel="Precision")
for ax in axes:
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
    ax.legend(fontsize=6.5, loc="best")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
--- 8 code ---
prob = val[SEL].to_numpy()
y = val["target"].to_numpy()
pred = (prob >= THR).astype(int)
tn, fp, fn, tp = confusion_matrix(y, pred, labels=[0, 1]).ravel()
out = pd.DataFrame({
    "metric": ["precision", "recall", "f1", "accuracy", "flagged", "tp", "fp", "fn", "tn"],
    "value": [tp / max(tp + fp, 1), tp / max(tp + fn, 1),
              2 * tp / max(2 * tp + fp + fn, 1), (tp + tn) / len(y), pred.mean(),
              tp, fp, fn, tn],
})
display(out.round(4))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4, 3.2))
ConfusionMatrixDisplay(np.array([[tn, fp], [fn, tp]]),
                       display_labels=["No buy", "Buy"]).plot(
    ax=ax, colorbar=False, cmap="Blues")
ax.set_title(f"{SEL} @ {THR:.3f}")
plt.show()
--- 9 markdown ---
## 3. Deep-learning model

A 256-128-64 MLP with batch norm, dropout, class-weighted BCE, AdamW and early stopping,
averaged over three seeds. The chart shows validation PR-AUC per epoch; early stopping
restored each seed's best epoch.
--- 10 code ---
log = pd.read_csv(REPORTS / "mlp_training_log.csv")
pivot = log.pivot_table(index="epoch", columns="seed", values="val_ap")
pivot.plot(figsize=(9, 4), marker="o", ms=2.5)
plt.title("MLP validation PR-AUC by epoch and seed")
plt.xlabel("epoch")
plt.ylabel("validation PR-AUC")
plt.grid(alpha=0.25)
plt.legend(title="seed")
plt.show()
--- 11 markdown ---
## 4. Feature importance

transformed feature is shuffled). Behavioural recency and frequency dominate, which matches
the retention domain.
--- 12 code ---
imp = pd.read_csv(REPORTS / "feature_importance_hgb.csv").head(18).iloc[::-1]
imp.plot.barh(x="feature", y="importance", figsize=(9, 5.2), legend=False, color="#2c6fbb")
plt.title("Top permutation importances (HGB, validation PR-AUC drop)")
plt.xlabel("drop in PR-AUC")
plt.grid(axis="x", alpha=0.25)
plt.tight_layout()

## 5. Segment and fairness analysis

Because the data is a sample, analysis is done at segment level. The tier snapshot shows how
a large low-propensity group (Bronze) differs from a small high-propensity group (Platinum).
The multi-group table then intersects conditions - for example Bronze AND active AND high
session volume, or email opt-in AND high sessions - so we can see which combinations carry
the expected buyers.
--- 14 code ---
test = pd.read_pickle(FEAT / "test_features.pkl")
probs = pd.read_csv(REPORTS / "test_probabilities.csv")
tv = probs[["customer_id", "selected_probability"]].merge(
    test[["customer_id", "cust_country", "cust_tier", "pref_email_opt", "pref_dnc",
          "sup_open_n", "sup_recent_complaint", "sup_n", "cust_loyalty", "tenure_days",
          "sess_n_180d", "sess_days_since_last", "txn_spend_180d", "txn_days_since_last"]],
    on="customer_id")
tv["flagged"] = tv["selected_probability"] >= THR
tv["recency_band"] = np.select(
    [tv["sess_days_since_last"].isna(), tv["sess_days_since_last"] <= 7,
     tv["sess_days_since_last"] <= 30, tv["sess_days_since_last"] <= 90],
    ["No session", "Active <=7d", "Warm 8-30d", "Cooling 31-90d"], default="Dormant >90d")
tv["loyalty_band"] = pd.qcut(tv["cust_loyalty"].rank(method="first"), 4,
                             labels=["Q1 low", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4 high"])
tv["session_band"] = pd.qcut(tv["sess_n_180d"].rank(method="first"), 4,
                             labels=["Q1 low", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4 high"])
tv["spend_band"] = pd.qcut(tv["txn_spend_180d"].rank(method="first"), 4,
                           labels=["Q1 low", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4 high"])


def summarize(frame, by):
    g = frame.groupby(by, observed=True).agg(
        customers=("selected_probability", "size"),
        mean_propensity=("selected_probability", "mean"),
        expected_buyers=("selected_probability", "sum"),
        flag_rate=("selected_probability", lambda s: (s >= THR).mean()))
    g["share_expected"] = g["expected_buyers"] / frame["selected_probability"].sum()
    return g.sort_values("expected_buyers", ascending=False)


print("Tier snapshot (test sample)")
display(summarize(tv, "cust_tier").round(3))
print("Country snapshot (test sample)")
display(summarize(tv, "cust_country").round(3))

segments = {
    "Bronze + active + high sessions": (tv["cust_tier"] == "Bronze") & (tv["recency_band"] == "Active <=7d") & (tv["session_band"] == "Q4 high"),
    "Email opt-in + high sessions": (tv["pref_email_opt"] == 1) & (tv["session_band"] == "Q4 high"),
    "Bronze + email opt-in": (tv["cust_tier"] == "Bronze") & (tv["pref_email_opt"] == 1),
    "High loyalty + cooling": (tv["loyalty_band"] == "Q4 high") & (tv["recency_band"] == "Cooling 31-90d"),
    "Gold/Silver + recent complaint": tv["cust_tier"].isin(["Gold", "Silver"]) & (tv["sup_recent_complaint"] == 1),
    "High spend + dormant": (tv["spend_band"] == "Q4 high") & (tv["recency_band"] == "Dormant >90d"),
    "Platinum + dormant": (tv["cust_tier"] == "Platinum") & (tv["recency_band"] == "Dormant >90d"),
    "Open complaint (all tiers)": tv["sup_open_n"].fillna(0) > 0,
    "DNC customers": tv["pref_dnc"] == 1,
}
rows = []
total = tv["selected_probability"].sum()
for name, mask in segments.items():
    s = tv.loc[mask, "selected_probability"]
    rows.append({"segment": name, "customers": len(s), "mean_propensity": s.mean(),
                 "expected_buyers": s.sum(), "share_expected": s.sum() / total,
                 "flag_rate": (s >= THR).mean() if len(s) else np.nan})
print("\nMulti-group intersections (test sample)")
display(pd.DataFrame(rows).sort_values("expected_buyers", ascending=False).round(3))

"""Regression tests for the Week 8 model checkpoint deliverable.

These tests are cheap: they validate the saved artifacts and the helpers that
produce them rather than retraining the model.  Tests that need generated
artifacts skip cleanly when the pipeline has not been run yet.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import pytest

from shopsphere.data.asof_time import black_friday, window_bounds
from shopsphere.data.build_features import days_since, to01

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
FEATURES = ROOT / "artifacts" / "features"
FIXED_REPORTS = ROOT / "artifacts" / "reports" / "fixed"
SUBMISSION = ROOT / "artifacts" / "outputs" / "submission.csv"
NOTEBOOK = ROOT / "notebooks" / "Week8_ShopSphere_Model_Checkpoint.ipynb"
CLEAN = ROOT / "data" / "clean"


def test_to01_handles_mixed_true_false_encodings():
    result = to01(pd.Series(["TRUE", "false", "Y", "no", "1", "0", None]))
    assert result.tolist()[:6] == [1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0]
    assert pd.isna(result.iloc[6])


def test_days_since_uses_as_of():
    dates = pd.Series(["2024-09-01", "2024-09-30"])
    assert days_since(dates, pd.Timestamp("2024-09-30")).tolist() == [29, 0]


def test_window_bounds_and_black_friday():
    start, end = window_bounds(pd.Timestamp("2024-09-30"), 30)
    assert start == pd.Timestamp("2024-10-01")
    assert end == pd.Timestamp("2024-10-30")
    assert black_friday(2024) == pd.Timestamp("2024-11-29")


@pytest.mark.skipif(not (FEATURES / "train_features.pkl").exists(), reason="features not built")
def test_feature_artifacts_match_metadata():
    meta = json.loads((FEATURES / "feature_metadata.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    train = pd.read_pickle(FEATURES / "train_features.pkl")
    test = pd.read_pickle(FEATURES / "test_features.pkl")
    assert len(train) == 64000
    assert len(test) == 16000
    assert meta["n_features"] == 180
    assert len(meta["feature_columns"]) == meta["n_features"]
    assert set(meta["feature_columns"]).issubset(train.columns)
    assert set(meta["feature_columns"]).issubset(test.columns)
    assert set(train["target"].unique()) <= {0, 1}
    assert not set(train["customer_id"]) & set(test["customer_id"])


@pytest.mark.skipif(not SUBMISSION.exists(), reason="submission not generated")
def test_submission_is_valid_and_matches_metrics():
    metrics = json.loads((FIXED_REPORTS / "metrics.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    submission = pd.read_csv(SUBMISSION)
    test_ids = pd.read_csv(CLEAN / "test.csv")["customer_id"]
    assert list(submission.columns) == ["customer_id", "target"]
    assert len(submission) == len(test_ids) == 16000
    assert submission["customer_id"].is_unique
    assert set(submission["customer_id"]) == set(test_ids)
    assert set(submission["target"].unique()) <= {0, 1}
    assert int(submission["target"].sum()) == metrics["submission_positives"]


@pytest.mark.skipif(not NOTEBOOK.exists(), reason="notebook missing")
def test_checkpoint_notebook_is_valid_and_error_free():
    nb = json.loads(NOTEBOOK.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    code_cells = [c for c in nb["cells"] if c["cell_type"] == "code"]
    assert code_cells
    assert all(c.get("execution_count") is not None for c in code_cells)
    errors = [
        output
        for cell in code_cells
        for output in cell.get("outputs", [])
        if output.get("output_type") == "error"
    ]
    assert not errors

Now check other potential issues for Week 8 fulfillment.

The brief says "supervised deep learning model trained on the data pack to predict the target in train.csv, evaluated properly and compared fairly against at least one non-deep-learning baseline". The fixed model does that. Good.

But there may be a data leakage concern: `build_features.py` uses `transaction_items` merged with `txn` which is filtered txn <= as_of, so okay. `deliveries` in build_features is not filtered by date — it merges all deliveries (including after cutoff) with txn_events (which only includes txn <= as_of), so deliveries linked to transactions after as_of are dropped because transaction_id not in txn_events. But deliveries for transactions before as_of might have delivered after as_of; that's arguably okay (delivery outcome known by as_of? no, delivered_date could be after cutoff). This is subtle leakage: delivery status/delay known at cutoff should only include deliveries that occurred/shipped before as_of. import json, warnings, numpy as np, pandas as pd

from sklearn.preprocessing import OrdinalEncoder

train=pd.read_pickle('artifacts/features/train_features.pkl')
meta=json.load(open('artifacts/features/feature_metadata.json'))
feats=meta['feature_columns']; cats=meta['categorical']; nums=[c for c in feats if c not in cats]
y=train['target'].to_numpy()

def add_feats(d):
    d=d.copy(); eps=1.0
    d['sess_per_day']=d['sess_n']/(d['tenure_days']+eps)
    d['spend_per_session']=d['txn_value_sum']/(d['sess_n']+eps)
    d['orders_per_session']=d['txn_n']/(d['sess_n']+eps)
    d['spend_per_order']=d['txn_value_sum']/(d['txn_n']+eps)
    d['cart_per_session']=d['sess_cart_sum']/(d['sess_n']+eps)
    d['recent_session_share']=d['sess_n_30d']/(d['sess_n']+eps)
    d['recent_order_share']=d['txn_n_30d']/(d['txn_n']+eps)
    d['recent_spend_share']=d['txn_spend_30d']/(d['txn_value_sum']+eps)
    d['recent90_spend_share']=d['txn_spend_90d']/(d['txn_value_sum']+eps)
    d['recency_x_loyalty']=d['cust_loyalty']/(d['sess_days_since_last']+eps)
    d['sessions_x_email']=d['sess_n_180d']*d['pref_email_opt']
    d['oct_x_dormant']=d['txn_oct_share']*(d['sess_days_since_last'].fillna(9999)>90).astype(int)
    d['holiday_x_dormant']=d['txn_holiday_share']*(d['sess_days_since_last'].fillna(9999)>90).astype(int)
    d['open_ticket_ratio']=d['sup_open_n']/(d['sup_n']+eps)
    d['recent_complaint_per_ticket']=d['sup_recent_complaint']/(d['sup_n']+eps)
    d['late_x_orders']=d['del_late_rate'].fillna(0)*d['del_n']
    d['lost_x_orders']=d['del_lost_rate'].fillna(0)*d['del_n']
    d['redeem_per_contact']=d['ret_redeemed_n']/(d['ret_n']+eps)
    d['no_session']=d['sess_days_since_last'].isna().astype(int)
    d['no_txn']=d['txn_days_since_last'].isna().astype(int)
    d['min_recency']=d[['sess_days_since_last','txn_days_since_last']].min(axis=1)
    d['max_recency']=d[['sess_days_since_last','txn_days_since_last']].max(axis=1)
    for c in ['cust_country','cust_region','cust_tier','pref_channel','pref_language','geo_tier']:
        d[c+'_freq']=d[c].map(d[c].value_counts(normalize=True))
    return d

def best_thr(y,p):
    pr,re,th=precision_recall_curve(y,p); f1=2*pr*re/np.maximum(pr+re,1e-9); i=np.nanargmax(f1)
    return float(th[i]) if i<len(th) else 0.5, float(f1[i])
def acc_best(y,p):
    qs=np.unique(np.quantile(p,np.linspace(0.01,0.99,99))); best=(-1,None)
    for t in qs:
        a=((p>=t).astype(int)==y).mean()
        if a>best[0]: best=(a,t)
    return best

# Project Brief: Win Back the Customer

IT2226 AI Innovation and Deep Learning Project  \|  Team project (4 students)  \|  Duration: 17 weeks

## 1. About this project

Your team will act as an AI solutions team engaged by an online retailer. You will study the business situation, explore and prepare the company's data, and design, build and evaluate an AI solution that helps the company's staff make better decisions.

The project assesses your ability to apply two areas of AI together:

- Supervised deep learning: training, evaluating and justifying a deep learning model on the data provided.

- Agentic AI: building an AI agent that reasons, uses tools (including your trained model) and takes actions to help staff solve real business problems.

This brief describes the client, its current situation, the problem, and what its staff wish for. It deliberately does not tell you how to solve the problem. Choosing an approach and justifying it is part of what you are assessed on.

| Item | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Team size | 4 students |
| Duration | 16 weeks |
| Client (fictional) | ShopSphere Global, an online retailer |
| Data | ShopSphere data pack: 17 data tables and 4 policy documents (see section 7) |

## 2. Client background

ShopSphere Global (a fictional company created for this project) is an online retailer founded in 2022. It sells about 400 products in eight categories (Electronics, Fashion, Home & Living, Beauty, Sports & Outdoors, Toys & Kids, Groceries, and Books & Media) to customers in the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, France and India, through its website and mobile app.

The company has grown quickly. Revenue is strongly seasonal: November (Singles' Day and Black Friday) and December are its busiest months. Its customers belong to a four-tier loyalty programme, ShopSphere Rewards (Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum).

## 3. The current situation

ShopSphere's leadership team is worried. The business keeps signing up new customers, but about one in three customers who have signed up have not visited the site at all in the last 90 days. Marketing spend keeps rising, while nobody can say with confidence which spending is working. The teaching team interviewed staff across the company, and their comments are summarised below.

### 3.1 CRM and Retention team

Every Monday, two CRM executives build the week's "win-back" list. They export data from the customer database, the order system, the preference centre and the helpdesk into spreadsheets, match them by hand, and choose customers mainly by how long it has been since their last order. Most customers on the list receive the same 10% voucher. Building the list takes about a day and a half.

> What staff say
> "By the time the list is ready, it's already out of date. And we keep giving vouchers to people who would have bought anyway." (CRM Manager)
> "Last quarter we sent a 20% voucher to Bronze customers by mistake. The policy says Platinum only. Nobody noticed for weeks." (CRM Executive)

### 3.2 Marketing

Marketing runs Email, Search, Display, Social and Affiliate campaigns, each targeted at a region. Results are reported in a monthly slide deck put together from the marketing platform's exports. The team cannot easily compare channels, regions or seasons.

> What staff say
> "I need to see, at a glance, what's trending and which campaigns pay back. Right now I find out a month later." (Head of Marketing)

### 3.3 Customer Service

About 30 agents handle email, live chat, phone and WhatsApp tickets. Volumes roughly double in November and December. To reply properly, agents have to look up the customer's orders, deliveries and earlier tickets in three different systems.

> What staff say
> "A customer whose parcel was lost got a 'We miss you, here's 10% off' email the same day they complained. That's how we lose people." (Customer Service Lead)

### 3.4 Operations

ShopSphere ships through seven carriers. Late deliveries are tracked, but the information isn't linked to customer behaviour.

> What staff say
> "I suspect some carriers are costing us customers, not just money. I can't prove it." (Operations Manager)

### 3.5 Merchandising and Finance

> What staff say
> "Marketing promoted a product we had zero stock of, and discounted items with margins too thin to discount." (Merchandising Lead)
> "Each country gets a weekly retention budget. I want to know before the money is spent that it's going to the right customers, and afterwards whether it worked." (Finance Controller)

## 4. Problem statement

> Problem statement
> ShopSphere's staff make important weekly decisions (who to re-engage, how, with which offer and through which channel) without knowing which customers are likely to purchase soon and which are drifting away. The information they need is spread across separate systems and policy documents, and pulling it together by hand is slow, inconsistent and error-prone. Managers also lack a timely view of the trends that would tell them whether these decisions are working.
> How might ShopSphere use its customer, behavioural and operational data, together with AI, to predict which customers will make a purchase in the next 30 days, and help its staff turn that prediction into timely, consistent, policy-compliant and cost-effective decisions?

## 5. Stakeholder wish list

The wish list below comes from ShopSphere's stakeholders. It is a list of needs, not a specification. You must explain which items you chose to address, which you did not, and why.

| # | Wish | Raised by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W1 | Know which customers are likely to make a purchase in the next 30 days. | CRM Manager |
| W2 | Understand why a customer is likely or unlikely to purchase, in terms staff can act on. | CRM Manager, Country Managers |
| W3 | Each week, get a recommended re-engagement list (who to contact, which offer, which channel) that stays within each country's budget. | CRM Manager, Finance Controller |
| W4 | Be certain every recommendation follows company policy: consent, contact frequency, open complaints, tier eligibility, stock and margin. | CRM Manager, Customer Service Lead |
| W5 | Before replying, give a customer service agent a one-screen summary of the customer: orders, deliveries, earlier tickets and any recent offers. | Customer Service Lead |
| W6 | A dashboard showing trends in sales, traffic, campaign performance, delivery performance and customer activity, by country and over time. | Head of Marketing, Operations Manager, Leadership |
| W7 | Ask business questions in plain language and get one answer that pulls together information from several sources. | Leadership, Finance Controller |
| W8 | Draft personalised messages in the customer's preferred language and channel. | CRM Executive |
| W9 | Keep humans in control: nothing is sent without approval, and every decision has a recorded reason. | CRM Manager |
| W10 | After a campaign, find out whether the money spent made a difference. | Finance Controller |

## 6. Project requirements

Whatever approach you choose, your solution must:

1. include a supervised deep learning model trained on the data pack to predict the target in train.csv, evaluated properly and compared fairly against at least one non-deep-learning baseline;

2. include an agentic AI component that uses your trained model as part of its reasoning or actions;

3. address at least five wish-list items, including W1, W3 and W6;

4. use information from at least four different tables or documents in the data pack when making a decision;

5. be demonstrated as a working prototype that ShopSphere staff could realistically use;

6. be evaluated with evidence: both the model and the agent;

7. consider responsible AI: fairness, privacy and consent, transparency, and the risk of the system being wrong.

## 7. The data pack

The data pack is ShopSphere's data extract as at 30 September 2024. The target in train.csv shows whether each customer made at least one purchase between 1 and 30 October 2024. All the data is synthetic and contains no real personal information.

The core tables follow the structure of the Kaggle competition Global E-Commerce Customer Purchase Prediction. They have been regenerated and extended by the NYP teaching team to reflect ShopSphere's operations. The full data dictionary is in Appendix A and in DATA_README.md in the data pack.

| Group | Files | What they describe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customer | customers.csv, customer_preferences.csv, geo_data.csv | Profiles, loyalty tier, consent and contact preferences, regional socio-economic data |
| Behaviour | sessions.csv, transactions.csv, transaction_items.csv | Browsing sessions, orders and order lines, January 2022 to September 2024 |
| Marketing | marketing_campaigns.csv, campaign_daily_performance.csv, retention_contact_history.csv | Campaigns (completed, active and planned), daily spend and results, retention offers sent |
| Operations | products.csv, deliveries.csv, support_tickets.csv | Catalogue, stock and margin; shipments and delays; customer service tickets with customers' messages |
| Finance and CRM | offer_catalogue.csv, retention_budget_2024Q4.csv | Allowed retention offers; weekly budget per country for Q4 2024 |
| Labels | train.csv, test.csv, sample_submission.csv | 64,000 labelled customers; 16,000 customers to predict |
| Policies | retention_offer_policy.md, shipping_and_returns_policy.md, customer_service_sla.md, loyalty_programme.md | ShopSphere's business rules |

> Watch out: The data is messy
> Like real company data, the pack contains inconsistent spellings, several encodings for true/false, numbers stored as text, missing values, outliers and duplicates. Some tables were exported by different systems. Treat data preparation as a real part of the project, and check the data itself rather than relying only on the documentation.

You may create additional synthetic data if your solution needs it. Any data you create must be documented and clearly labelled as synthetic. The data pack itself must not be altered.

## 8. Deliverables and milestones

| Week | Deliverable | What it must contain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | Project proposal (max 6 pages) and 10-minute pitch | Stakeholders and their needs; the wish-list items chosen and why; initial data exploration and data quality findings; proposed approach; plan and roles; risks. |
| 8 | Model checkpoint (short report + notebook) | Data preparation and feature pipeline, baseline(s), deep learning model(s), evaluation, a first test-set submission, and the model you intend to use, with justification. |
| 13 | Prototype demonstration (15 minutes, live) | Working end-to-end prototype, including the dashboard, demonstrated on realistic ShopSphere scenarios, with early evaluation results. |
| 16 | Final report (max 25 pages + appendices) | Problem, data, model development and evaluation, agent and dashboard design and evaluation, responsible AI, results against the wish list, limitations, future work. |
| 16 | Final presentation and live demo (20 minutes + Q&A) | Presented to a panel acting as ShopSphere leadership. Every member presents. |
| 16 | Code repository and final test-set submission | Reproducible code, notebooks and README. No API keys committed. |
| 16 | Individual reflection and peer evaluation | Each member's contribution and learning; an evaluation of teammates' contributions. |

## 9. Teamwork, constraints and rules

- Each member must own at least one major component and be able to explain it in Q&A.

- Use Git from Week 1 and keep a shared task board and weekly meeting log.

- Use only open-source libraries and the AI models or APIs your lecturer approves. Stay within any API budget you are given.

- Declare any use of generative AI tools in your report: which tools you used and what for.

- Your prototype must not connect to any real messaging, email or payment system.

> "By the time the list is ready, it's already out of date. And we keep giving vouchers to people who would have bought anyway." (CRM Manager)
> "Last quarter we sent a 20% voucher to Bronze customers by mistake. The policy says Platinum only. Nobody noticed for weeks." (CRM Executive)

### 3.2 Marketing

Marketing runs Email, Search, Display, Social and Affiliate campaigns, each targeted at a region. Results are reported in a monthly slide deck put together from the marketing platform's exports. The team cannot easily compare channels, regions or seasons.

> What staff say
> "I need to see, at a glance, what's trending and which campaigns pay back. Right now I find out a month later." (Head of Marketing)

### 3.3 Customer Service

About 30 agents handle email, live chat, phone and WhatsApp tickets. Volumes roughly double in November and December. To reply properly, agents have to look up the customer's orders, deliveries and earlier tickets in three different systems.

> What staff say
> "A customer whose parcel was lost got a 'We miss you, here's 10% off' email the same day they complained. That's how we lose people." (Customer Service Lead)

### 3.4 Operations

ShopSphere ships through seven carriers. Late deliveries are tracked, but the information isn't linked to customer behaviour.

> What staff say
> "I suspect some carriers are costing us customers, not just money. I can't prove it." (Operations Manager)

### 3.5 Merchandising and Finance

> What staff say
> "Marketing promoted a product we had zero stock of, and discounted items with margins too thin to discount." (Merchandising Lead)
> "Each country gets a weekly retention budget. I want to know before the money is spent that it's going to the right customers, and afterwards whether it worked." (Finance Controller)

## 4. Problem statement

> Problem statement
> ShopSphere's staff make important weekly decisions (who to re-engage, how, with which offer and through which channel) without knowing which customers are likely to purchase soon and which are drifting away. The information they need is spread across separate systems and policy documents, and pulling it together by hand is slow, inconsistent and error-prone. Managers also lack a timely view of the trends that would tell them whether these decisions are working.
> How might ShopSphere use its customer, behavioural and operational data, together with AI, to predict which customers will make a purchase in the next 30 days, and help its staff turn that prediction into timely, consistent, policy-compliant and cost-effective decisions?

## 5. Stakeholder wish list

The wish list below comes from ShopSphere's stakeholders. It is a list of needs, not a specification. You must explain which items you chose to address, which you did not, and why.

| # | Wish | Raised by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W1 | Know which customers are likely to make a purchase in the next 30 days. | CRM Manager |
| W2 | Understand why a customer is likely or unlikely to purchase, in terms staff can act on. | CRM Manager, Country Managers |
| W3 | Each week, get a recommended re-engagement list (who to contact, which offer, which channel) that stays within each country's budget. | CRM Manager, Finance Controller |
| W4 | Be certain every recommendation follows company policy: consent, contact frequency, open complaints, tier eligibility, stock and margin. | CRM Manager, Customer Service Lead |
| W5 | Before replying, give a customer service agent a one-screen summary of the customer: orders, deliveries, earlier tickets and any recent offers. | Customer Service Lead |
| W6 | A dashboard showing trends in sales, traffic, campaign performance, delivery performance and customer activity, by country and over time. | Head of Marketing, Operations Manager, Leadership |
| W7 | Ask business questions in plain language and get one answer that pulls together information from several sources. | Leadership, Finance Controller |
| W8 | Draft personalised messages in the customer's preferred language and channel. | CRM Executive |
| W9 | Keep humans in control: nothing is sent without approval, and every decision has a recorded reason. | CRM Manager |
| W10 | After a campaign, find out whether the money spent made a difference. | Finance Controller |

Whatever approach you choose, your solution must:

1. include a supervised deep learning model trained on the data pack to predict the target in train.csv, evaluated properly and compared fairly against at least one non-deep-learning baseline;

2. include an agentic AI component that uses your trained model as part of its reasoning or actions;

3. address at least five wish-list items, including W1, W3 and W6;

4. use information from at least four different tables or documents in the data pack when making a decision;

5. be demonstrated as a working prototype that ShopSphere staff could realistically use;

6. be evaluated with evidence: both the model and the agent;

7. consider responsible AI: fairness, privacy and consent, transparency, and the risk of the system being wrong.

## 7. The data pack

The data pack is ShopSphere's data extract as at 30 September 2024. The target in train.csv shows whether each customer made at least one purchase between 1 and 30 October 2024. All the data is synthetic and contains no real personal information.

The core tables follow the structure of the Kaggle competition Global E-Commerce Customer Purchase Prediction. They have been regenerated and extended by the NYP teaching team to reflect ShopSphere's operations. The full data dictionary is in Appendix A and in DATA_README.md in the data pack.

R=42

feats=meta['feature_columns']; cats=meta['categorical']; y=train.target.to_numpy()

def score(y,p):
    ap=average_precision_score(y,p); auc=roc_auc_score(y,p); pr,re,th=precision_recall_curve(y,p); f1=2*pr*re/np.maximum(pr+re,1e-9); i=np.nanargmax(f1); t=float(th[i]) if i<len(th) else .5; return ap,auc,f1[i],t,((p>=t).astype(int)==y).mean()
def predict(m,X,batch=4096):
    m.eval(); out=[]
    with torch.no_grad():
        for i in range(0,len(X),batch): out.append(torch.sigmoid(m(torch.from_numpy(X[i:i+batch]))).numpy())
    return np.concatenate(out)
def train_variant(label,hidden,dropout,lr,wd,pos_weight_mult=1.0,seeds=[42,7,2024],epochs=40,patience=8,bs=512):
    preds=[]; t0=time.time()
    for seed in seeds:
        torch.manual_seed(seed); m=MLP(Xtr.shape[1],hidden=hidden,dropout=dropout)
        pw=torch.tensor([(len(ytr)-ytr.sum())/max(ytr.sum(),1)*pos_weight_mult],dtype=torch.float32)
        crit=nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss(pos_weight=pw); opt=torch.optim.AdamW(m.parameters(),lr=lr,weight_decay=wd); sched=torch.optim.lr_scheduler.ReduceLROnPlateau(opt,mode='max',factor=.5,patience=3)

        best=(-1,None,0); wait=0
        for ep in range(1,epochs+1):
            m.train()
            for xb,yb in dl:
                opt.zero_grad(); loss=crit(m(xb),yb); loss.backward(); opt.step()
            pv=predict(m,Xva); ap=average_precision_score(yva,pv); sched.step(ap)

    return p

train_variant('current lower pos_weight 0.5',(256,128,64),(.35,.30,.20),1e-3,1e-4,pos_weight_mult=.5)

- n=80,000

- actual positives = n*p
- precision = tp/(tp+fp)
- recall = tp/(actual positives)
- predicted positives = tp/precision
- tp = recall * actual positives
- fp = predicted positives - tp
- fn = actual positives - tp
- tn = n - tp - fp - fn

    "target_is_christmas_window", "target_peak_proximity",
)


def load_scores() -> pd.DataFrame:
    return pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(OUT_DATA, "offer_candidate_scores.parquet"))


def default_week_start() -> pd.Timestamp:
    budget = read_budget()
    weeks = pd.to_datetime(budget["week_start"]).dropna().sort_values().unique()
    if not len(weeks):
        return pd.Timestamp(resolve_as_of(None, DATA_DIR)) + pd.Timedelta(days=7)
    as_of = pd.Timestamp(resolve_as_of(None, DATA_DIR))
    upcoming = [w for w in weeks if pd.Timestamp(w) >= as_of]
    return pd.Timestamp(upcoming[0] if upcoming else weeks[-1])


def budget_for(week_start, country: str) -> float:
    budget = read_budget()

    row = budget[(budget["week_start"] == week) & (budget["country"] == country)]
    if len(row):
        return float(row["retention_budget_usd"].iloc[0])
    nearest = budget[budget["country"] == country]
    if len(nearest):
        nearest = nearest.assign(_gap=(nearest["week_start"] - week).abs())
        return float(nearest.sort_values("_gap")["retention_budget_usd"].iloc[0])
    return float(budget["retention_budget_usd"].mean())


def _scalar(value):
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and np.isnan(value)):
        return None
    if hasattr(value, "item"):
        return value.item()
    return value


def _date_str(value):
    return str(pd.Timestamp(value).date()) if value is not None else None


def score_window_context(scores: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:
    """Read the rolling W1 as-of/target-window context from the score table."""
    if scores is None or scores.empty:

    out = {}

def _month_seasonality_factor(week_start, country: str, horizon_days: int):

    df["expected_incremental_margin"] *= seasonal_factor
    df["expected_net_value"] = df["expected_incremental_margin"] - df["offer_cost"]
    df["roi"] = (
        df["expected_net_value"] / df["offer_cost"].replace(0, pd.NA)
    )

        (week - pd.to_datetime(df["last_contact_date"])).dt.days.fillna(9999)
    )
    df = df[df["days_since_last_contact"] >= cooldown_days].copy()
    df = df[df["uplift"] >= min_uplift].copy()
    df = df[df["expected_incremental_revenue"] > 0].copy()
    if min_net_value is not None:
        df = df[df["expected_net_value"] >= min_net_value].copy()
    if objective == "roi":
        df = df[(df["expected_net_value"] > 0) & (df["offer_cost"] > 0)].copy()
    elif objective == "net_value":
        df = df[df["expected_net_value"] > 0].copy()

    if objective in ("incremental_revenue", "propensity"):
        df["priority_score"] = df["expected_incremental_revenue"]
    elif objective == "net_value":
        df["priority_score"] = df["expected_net_value"]
    else:
        df["priority_score"] = df["roi"]

    df = df.sort_values(["priority_score", "expected_net_value"], ascending=False)
    df = df.drop_duplicates("sample_ref", keep="first").copy()
    df = df.sort_values(["priority_score", "expected_net_value"], ascending=False)

    budget = float(budget_usd) if budget_usd is not None else budget_for(week, country)
    cumulative = df["offer_cost"].cumsum()
    df = df[cumulative <= budget].copy()
    if max_contacts is not None:
        df = df.head(int(max_contacts)).copy()

    df.insert(0, "week_start", week.date().isoformat())
    df.insert(1, "country", country)
    df["priority_rank"] = range(1, len(df) + 1)

    spend = float(df["offer_cost"].sum())
    inc_rev = float(df["expected_incremental_revenue"].sum())
    inc_margin = float(df["expected_incremental_margin"].sum())
    net = float(df["expected_net_value"].sum())
    score_as_of = scores["w1_as_of"].iloc[0] if "w1_as_of" in scores else None
    score_window_start = scores["w1_window_start"].iloc[0] if "w1_window_start" in scores else None
    score_window_end = scores["w1_window_end"].iloc[0] if "w1_window_end" in scores else None
    rolling_meta_path = os.path.join(ROLLING_MODELS, "rolling_meta.json")
    score_model = None
    if os.path.exists(rolling_meta_path):
        with open(rolling_meta_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            score_model = json.load(fh).get("selected_model")
    summary = {
        "week_start": week.date().isoformat(),
        "week_end": (week + pd.Timedelta(days=6)).date().isoformat(),
        "country": country,
        "objective": objective,
        "score_as_of": str(pd.Timestamp(score_as_of).date()) if score_as_of is not None else None,
        "score_window_start": str(pd.Timestamp(score_window_start).date()) if score_window_start is not None else None,
        "score_window_end": str(pd.Timestamp(score_window_end).date()) if score_window_end is not None else None,
        "score_model": score_model,
        "target_window_start": _date_str(window_context.get("target_window_start")),
        "target_window_end": _date_str(window_context.get("target_window_end")),
        "target_month_start": _scalar(window_context.get("target_month_start")),
        "target_month_end": _scalar(window_context.get("target_month_end")),
        "target_is_holiday": _scalar(window_context.get("target_is_holiday")),
        "target_days_to_black_friday": _scalar(window_context.get("target_days_to_black_friday")),
        "target_days_to_christmas": _scalar(window_context.get("target_days_to_christmas")),
        "objective_label": OBJECTIVES[objective],

        "seasonal_factor": round(float(seasonal_factor), 4),
        "seasonal_note": seasonal_note,

        "expected_incremental_revenue": round(inc_rev, 2),
        "expected_incremental_margin": round(inc_margin, 2),
        "expected_net_value": round(net, 2),
        "expected_roi": round(net / spend, 4) if spend else None,
        "avg_uplift": round(float(df["uplift"].mean()), 5) if len(df) else None,
        "avg_purchase_probability": round(float(df["purchase_probability"].mean()), 5) if len(df) else None,
        "avg_w1_probability": round(float(df["w1_probability"].mean()), 5) if len(df) else None,
        "offer_mix": df["offer_code"].value_counts().to_dict() if len(df) else {},
        "channel_mix": df["channel"].value_counts().to_dict() if len(df) else {},
        "tier_mix": df["cust_tier"].value_counts().to_dict() if len(df) else {},
    }
    return df, summary


def main() -> None:
    ensure_dirs()
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--week", default=None,
                        help="Planning week (default: first budget week on/after latest data date)")
    parser.add_argument("--country", default="US")
    parser.add_argument("--objective", default="incremental_revenue", choices=sorted(OBJECTIVES))
    parser.add_argument("--budget", type=float, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--min-uplift", type=float, default=0.0)
    parser.add_argument("--max-contacts", type=int, default=None)

    print(plan.head(10).to_string(index=False))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    print(json.dumps(summary, indent=2))
    print(plan.head(10).to_string(index=False))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

- W1 model predicts who will buy anyway. That's used as a ranking tool and a baseline.
