1: # Project Brief: Win Back the Customer
2: 
3: IT2226 AI Innovation and Deep Learning Project  \|  Team project (4 students)  \|  Duration: 17 weeks
4: 
5: ## 1. About this project
6: 
7: Your team will act as an AI solutions team engaged by an online retailer. You will study the business situation, explore and prepare the company's data, and design, build and evaluate an AI solution that helps the company's staff make better decisions.
8: 
9: The project assesses your ability to apply two areas of AI together:
10: 
11: - Supervised deep learning: training, evaluating and justifying a deep learning model on the data provided.
12: 
13: - Agentic AI: building an AI agent that reasons, uses tools (including your trained model) and takes actions to help staff solve real business problems.
14: 
15: This brief describes the client, its current situation, the problem, and what its staff wish for. It deliberately does not tell you how to solve the problem. Choosing an approach and justifying it is part of what you are assessed on.
16: 
17: | Item | Details |
18: | --- | --- |
19: | Team size | 4 students |
20: | Duration | 16 weeks |
21: | Client (fictional) | ShopSphere Global, an online retailer |
22: | Data | ShopSphere data pack: 17 data tables and 4 policy documents (see section 7) |
23: 
24: ## 2. Client background
25: 
26: ShopSphere Global (a fictional company created for this project) is an online retailer founded in 2022. It sells about 400 products in eight categories (Electronics, Fashion, Home & Living, Beauty, Sports & Outdoors, Toys & Kids, Groceries, and Books & Media) to customers in the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, France and India, through its website and mobile app.
27: 
28: The company has grown quickly. Revenue is strongly seasonal: November (Singles' Day and Black Friday) and December are its busiest months. Its customers belong to a four-tier loyalty programme, ShopSphere Rewards (Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum).
29: 
30: ## 3. The current situation
31: 
32: ShopSphere's leadership team is worried. The business keeps signing up new customers, but about one in three customers who have signed up have not visited the site at all in the last 90 days. Marketing spend keeps rising, while nobody can say with confidence which spending is working. The teaching team interviewed staff across the company, and their comments are summarised below.
33: 
34: ### 3.1 CRM and Retention team
35: 
36: Every Monday, two CRM executives build the week's "win-back" list. They export data from the customer database, the order system, the preference centre and the helpdesk into spreadsheets, match them by hand, and choose customers mainly by how long it has been since their last order. Most customers on the list receive the same 10% voucher. Building the list takes about a day and a half.
37: 
38: > What staff say
39: > "By the time the list is ready, it's already out of date. And we keep giving vouchers to people who would have bought anyway." (CRM Manager)
40: > "Last quarter we sent a 20% voucher to Bronze customers by mistake. The policy says Platinum only. Nobody noticed for weeks." (CRM Executive)
41: 
42: ### 3.2 Marketing
43: 
44: Marketing runs Email, Search, Display, Social and Affiliate campaigns, each targeted at a region. Results are reported in a monthly slide deck put together from the marketing platform's exports. The team cannot easily compare channels, regions or seasons.
45: 
46: > What staff say
47: > "I need to see, at a glance, what's trending and which campaigns pay back. Right now I find out a month later." (Head of Marketing)
48: 
49: ### 3.3 Customer Service
50: 
51: About 30 agents handle email, live chat, phone and WhatsApp tickets. Volumes roughly double in November and December. To reply properly, agents have to look up the customer's orders, deliveries and earlier tickets in three different systems.
52: 
53: > What staff say
54: > "A customer whose parcel was lost got a 'We miss you, here's 10% off' email the same day they complained. That's how we lose people." (Customer Service Lead)
55: 
56: ### 3.4 Operations
57: 
58: ShopSphere ships through seven carriers. Late deliveries are tracked, but the information isn't linked to customer behaviour.
59: 
60: > What staff say
61: > "I suspect some carriers are costing us customers, not just money. I can't prove it." (Operations Manager)
62: 
63: ### 3.5 Merchandising and Finance
64: 
65: > What staff say
66: > "Marketing promoted a product we had zero stock of, and discounted items with margins too thin to discount." (Merchandising Lead)
67: > "Each country gets a weekly retention budget. I want to know before the money is spent that it's going to the right customers, and afterwards whether it worked." (Finance Controller)
68: 
69: ## 4. Problem statement
70: 
71: > Problem statement
72: > ShopSphere's staff make important weekly decisions (who to re-engage, how, with which offer and through which channel) without knowing which customers are likely to purchase soon and which are drifting away. The information they need is spread across separate systems and policy documents, and pulling it together by hand is slow, inconsistent and error-prone. Managers also lack a timely view of the trends that would tell them whether these decisions are working.
73: > How might ShopSphere use its customer, behavioural and operational data, together with AI, to predict which customers will make a purchase in the next 30 days, and help its staff turn that prediction into timely, consistent, policy-compliant and cost-effective decisions?
74: 
75: ## 5. Stakeholder wish list
76: 
77: The wish list below comes from ShopSphere's stakeholders. It is a list of needs, not a specification. You must explain which items you chose to address, which you did not, and why.
78: 
79: | # | Wish | Raised by |
80: | --- | --- | --- |
81: | W1 | Know which customers are likely to make a purchase in the next 30 days. | CRM Manager |
82: | W2 | Understand why a customer is likely or unlikely to purchase, in terms staff can act on. | CRM Manager, Country Managers |
83: | W3 | Each week, get a recommended re-engagement list (who to contact, which offer, which channel) that stays within each country's budget. | CRM Manager, Finance Controller |
84: | W4 | Be certain every recommendation follows company policy: consent, contact frequency, open complaints, tier eligibility, stock and margin. | CRM Manager, Customer Service Lead |
85: | W5 | Before replying, give a customer service agent a one-screen summary of the customer: orders, deliveries, earlier tickets and any recent offers. | Customer Service Lead |
86: | W6 | A dashboard showing trends in sales, traffic, campaign performance, delivery performance and customer activity, by country and over time. | Head of Marketing, Operations Manager, Leadership |
87: | W7 | Ask business questions in plain language and get one answer that pulls together information from several sources. | Leadership, Finance Controller |
88: | W8 | Draft personalised messages in the customer's preferred language and channel. | CRM Executive |
89: | W9 | Keep humans in control: nothing is sent without approval, and every decision has a recorded reason. | CRM Manager |
90: | W10 | After a campaign, find out whether the money spent made a difference. | Finance Controller |
91: 
92: ## 6. Project requirements
93: 
94: Whatever approach you choose, your solution must:
95: 
96: 1. include a supervised deep learning model trained on the data pack to predict the target in train.csv, evaluated properly and compared fairly against at least one non-deep-learning baseline;
97: 
98: 2. include an agentic AI component that uses your trained model as part of its reasoning or actions;
99: 
100: 3. address at least five wish-list items, including W1, W3 and W6;
101: 
102: 4. use information from at least four different tables or documents in the data pack when making a decision;
103: 
104: 5. be demonstrated as a working prototype that ShopSphere staff could realistically use;
105: 
106: 6. be evaluated with evidence: both the model and the agent;
107:

# Project Brief: Win Back the Customer

IT2226 AI Innovation and Deep Learning Project  \|  Team project (4 students)  \|  Duration: 17 weeks

## 1. About this project

Your team will act as an AI solutions team engaged by an online retailer. You will study the business situation, explore and prepare the company's data, and design, build and evaluate an AI solution that helps the company's staff make better decisions.

The project assesses your ability to apply two areas of AI together:

- Supervised deep learning: training, evaluating and justifying a deep learning model on the data provided.

- Agentic AI: building an AI agent that reasons, uses tools (including your trained model) and takes actions to help staff solve real business problems.

This brief describes the client, its current situation, the problem, and what its staff wish for. It deliberately does not tell you how to solve the problem. Choosing an approach and justifying it is part of what you are assessed on.

| Item | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Team size | 4 students |
| Duration | 16 weeks |
| Client (fictional) | ShopSphere Global, an online retailer |
| Data | ShopSphere data pack: 17 data tables and 4 policy documents (see section 7) |

## 2. Client background

ShopSphere Global (a fictional company created for this project) is an online retailer founded in 2022. It sells about 400 products in eight categories (Electronics, Fashion, Home & Living, Beauty, Sports & Outdoors, Toys & Kids, Groceries, and Books & Media) to customers in the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, France and India, through its website and mobile app.

The company has grown quickly. Revenue is strongly seasonal: November (Singles' Day and Black Friday) and December are its busiest months. Its customers belong to a four-tier loyalty programme, ShopSphere Rewards (Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum).

## 3. The current situation

ShopSphere's leadership team is worried. The business keeps signing up new customers, but about one in three customers who have signed up have not visited the site at all in the last 90 days. Marketing spend keeps rising, while nobody can say with confidence which spending is working. The teaching team interviewed staff across the company, and their comments are summarised below.

### 3.1 CRM and Retention team

Every Monday, two CRM executives build the week's "win-back" list. They export data from the customer database, the order system, the preference centre and the helpdesk into spreadsheets, match them by hand, and choose customers mainly by how long it has been since their last order. Most customers on the list receive the same 10% voucher. Building the list takes about a day and a half.

> What staff say
> "By the time the list is ready, it's already out of date. And we keep giving vouchers to people who would have bought anyway." (CRM Manager)
> "Last quarter we sent a 20% voucher to Bronze customers by mistake. The policy says Platinum only. Nobody noticed for weeks." (CRM Executive)

### 3.2 Marketing

Marketing runs Email, Search, Display, Social and Affiliate campaigns, each targeted at a region. Results are reported in a monthly slide deck put together from the marketing platform's exports. The team cannot easily compare channels, regions or seasons.

> What staff say
> "I need to see, at a glance, what's trending and which campaigns pay back. Right now I find out a month later." (Head of Marketing)

### 3.3 Customer Service

About 30 agents handle email, live chat, phone and WhatsApp tickets. Volumes roughly double in November and December. To reply properly, agents have to look up the customer's orders, deliveries and earlier tickets in three different systems.

> What staff say
> "A customer whose parcel was lost got a 'We miss you, here's 10% off' email the same day they complained. That's how we lose people." (Customer Service Lead)

### 3.4 Operations

ShopSphere ships through seven carriers. Late deliveries are tracked, but the information isn't linked to customer behaviour.

> What staff say
> "I suspect some carriers are costing us customers, not just money. I can't prove it." (Operations Manager)

### 3.5 Merchandising and Finance

> What staff say
> "Marketing promoted a product we had zero stock of, and discounted items with margins too thin to discount." (Merchandising Lead)
> "Each country gets a weekly retention budget. I want to know before the money is spent that it's going to the right customers, and afterwards whether it worked." (Finance Controller)

## 4. Problem statement

> Problem statement
> ShopSphere's staff make important weekly decisions (who to re-engage, how, with which offer and through which channel) without knowing which customers are likely to purchase soon and which are drifting away. The information they need is spread across separate systems and policy documents, and pulling it together by hand is slow, inconsistent and error-prone. Managers also lack a timely view of the trends that would tell them whether these decisions are working.
> How might ShopSphere use its customer, behavioural and operational data, together with AI, to predict which customers will make a purchase in the next 30 days, and help its staff turn that prediction into timely, consistent, policy-compliant and cost-effective decisions?

## 5. Stakeholder wish list

The wish list below comes from ShopSphere's stakeholders. It is a list of needs, not a specification. You must explain which items you chose to address, which you did not, and why.

| # | Wish | Raised by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| W1 | Know which customers are likely to make a purchase in the next 30 days. | CRM Manager |
| W2 | Understand why a customer is likely or unlikely to purchase, in terms staff can act on. | CRM Manager, Country Managers |
| W3 | Each week, get a recommended re-engagement list (who to contact, which offer, which channel) that stays within each country's budget. | CRM Manager, Finance Controller |
| W4 | Be certain every recommendation follows company policy: consent, contact frequency, open complaints, tier eligibility, stock and margin. | CRM Manager, Customer Service Lead |
| W5 | Before replying, give a customer service agent a one-screen summary of the customer: orders, deliveries, earlier tickets and any recent offers. | Customer Service Lead |
| W6 | A dashboard showing trends in sales, traffic, campaign performance, delivery performance and customer activity, by country and over time. | Head of Marketing, Operations Manager, Leadership |
| W7 | Ask business questions in plain language and get one answer that pulls together information from several sources. | Leadership, Finance Controller |
| W8 | Draft personalised messages in the customer's preferred language and channel. | CRM Executive |
| W9 | Keep humans in control: nothing is sent without approval, and every decision has a recorded reason. | CRM Manager |
| W10 | After a campaign, find out whether the money spent made a difference. | Finance Controller |

## 6. Project requirements

Whatever approach you choose, your solution must:

1. include a supervised deep learning model trained on the data pack to predict the target in train.csv, evaluated properly and compared fairly against at least one non-deep-learning baseline;

2. include an agentic AI component that uses your trained model as part of its reasoning or actions;

3. address at least five wish-list items, including W1, W3 and W6;

4. use information from at least four different tables or documents in the data pack when making a decision;

5. be demonstrated as a working prototype that ShopSphere staff could realistically use;

6. be evaluated with evidence: both the model and the agent;

7. consider responsible AI: fairness, privacy and consent, transparency, and the risk of the system being wrong.

## 7. The data pack

The data pack is ShopSphere's data extract as at 30 September 2024. The target in train.csv shows whether each customer made at least one purchase between 1 and 30 October 2024. All the data is synthetic and contains no real personal information.

The core tables follow the structure of the Kaggle competition Global E-Commerce Customer Purchase Prediction. They have been regenerated and extended by the NYP teaching team to reflect ShopSphere's operations. The full data dictionary is in Appendix A and in DATA_README.md in the data pack.

| Group | Files | What they describe |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Customer | customers.csv, customer_preferences.csv, geo_data.csv | Profiles, loyalty tier, consent and contact preferences, regional socio-economic data |
| Behaviour | sessions.csv, transactions.csv, transaction_items.csv | Browsing sessions, orders and order lines, January 2022 to September 2024 |
| Marketing | marketing_campaigns.csv, campaign_daily_performance.csv, retention_contact_history.csv | Campaigns (completed, active and planned), daily spend and results, retention offers sent |
| Operations | products.csv, deliveries.csv, support_tickets.csv | Catalogue, stock and margin; shipments and delays; customer service tickets with customers' messages |
| Finance and CRM | offer_catalogue.csv, retention_budget_2024Q4.csv | Allowed retention offers; weekly budget per country for Q4 2024 |
| Labels | train.csv, test.csv, sample_submission.csv | 64,000 labelled customers; 16,000 customers to predict |
| Policies | retention_offer_policy.md, shipping_and_returns_policy.md, customer_service_sla.md, loyalty_programme.md | ShopSphere's business rules |

> Watch out: The data is messy
> Like real company data, the pack contains inconsistent spellings, several encodings for true/false, numbers stored as text, missing values, outliers and duplicates. Some tables were exported by different systems. Treat data preparation as a real part of the project, and check the data itself rather than relying only on the documentation.

You may create additional synthetic data if your solution needs it. Any data you create must be documented and clearly labelled as synthetic. The data pack itself must not be altered.

## 8. Deliverables and milestones

| Week | Deliverable | What it must contain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 | Project proposal (max 6 pages) and 10-minute pitch | Stakeholders and their needs; the wish-list items chosen and why; initial data exploration and data quality findings; proposed approach; plan and roles; risks. |
| 8 | Model checkpoint (short report + notebook) | Data preparation and feature pipeline, baseline(s), deep learning model(s), evaluation, a first test-set submission, and the model you intend to use, with justification. |
| 13 | Prototype demonstration (15 minutes, live) | Working end-to-end prototype, including the dashboard, demonstrated on realistic ShopSphere scenarios, with early evaluation results. |
| 16 | Final report (max 25 pages + appendices) | Problem, data, model development and evaluation, agent and dashboard design and evaluation, responsible AI, results against the wish list, limitations, future work. |
| 16 | Final presentation and live demo (20 minutes + Q&A) | Presented to a panel acting as ShopSphere leadership. Every member presents. |
| 16 | Code repository and final test-set submission | Reproducible code, notebooks and README. No API keys committed. |
| 16 | Individual reflection and peer evaluation | Each member's contribution and learning; an evaluation of teammates' contributions. |

## 9. Teamwork, constraints and rules

- Each member must own at least one major component and be able to explain it in Q&A.

- Use Git from Week 1 and keep a shared task board and weekly meeting log.

- Use only open-source libraries and the AI models or APIs your lecturer approves. Stay within any API budget you are given.

- Declare any use of generative AI tools in your report: which tools you used and what for.

- Your prototype must not connect to any real messaging, email or payment system.

## 10. Assessment

A detailed rubric will be released separately. Broadly, you will be assessed on:

- understanding of the stakeholders and the problem;

- data preparation and deep learning;

- agentic AI;

- the dashboard and analytics;

- evaluation;

- responsible AI;

- the prototype, report and presentation;

- individual contribution.

# ShopSphere Retention Intelligence

Rolling 30-day purchase propensity (W1), budgeted offer planning (W3),
performance analytics (W6), approval workflow (W9), and campaign effectiveness
(W10).

## Quick start

```powershell
py run_all.py
py -m streamlit run app.py
```

`run_all.py` builds the rolling W1 model when it is missing, prepares contact
features, trains the offer-response models, scores candidates, builds analytics
tables, and initializes the approval database. Set
`SHOPSPHERE_RETRAIN_ROLLING=1` to force a rolling-model rebuild, or
`SHOPSPHERE_SKIP_ROLLING=1` to reuse existing rolling artifacts.

## Layout

```
configs/                  runtime configuration examples
data/raw/            new raw files awaiting validation and cleaning
data/clean/               cleaned source CSVs; sole prediction input
data/processed/           generated customer, score, analytics, and approval data
artifacts/features/       fixed-model feature artifacts
artifacts/snapshots/      rolling as-of snapshots
artifacts/models/         fixed/, rolling/, and offer/ model artifacts
artifacts/reports/        fixed/, rolling/, offer/, analytics/, plans/, logs/
```

# ShopSphere - Week 8 Model Checkpoint Report

**Course:** IT2226 AI Innovation & Deep Learning  
**Project:** ShopSphere customer purchase propensity and retention outreach  
**Deliverable:** Week 8 checkpoint - model, evaluation, first test submission

> **Sample framing.** The dataset is a sample of the customer base, not a full census.
> Results describe segment-level tendencies and are not used to make decisions about
> individual customers. The analysis and dashboard contain no customer IDs or individual
> lookup.

## 1. Objective

Estimate the probability that a sampled customer purchases in the 30 days after the
**2024-09-30** data cutoff (October 2024 window) so retention effort can be prioritised by
segment. The modelling grain is one row per sampled customer: 64,000 training rows (14.6%
positive) and 16,000 disjoint test rows.

## 2. Data preparation and features

- Thirteen cleaned source tables are used (customers, customer preferences, geo data,
  sessions, transactions, transaction items, products, deliveries, support tickets, retention
  contacts, campaigns, campaign performance and the retention budget).
- Cleaning follows one convention: ISO dates, quoted booleans, `_clean` categorical fields,
  exact duplicates removed, invalid values blanked, IQR caps only on duration-like fields.
- **180 customer-level features** (174 numeric, 6 categorical) are built strictly from data
  on or before the cutoff, then one-hot encoded and scaled to a 294-column matrix.
- **Seasonality is modelled explicitly.** Because the data spans January 2022 to September
  2024, the pipeline adds historical October and Nov-Dec behaviour per customer: October
  transaction/session counts and shares, holiday-season shares, monthly seasonality indices,
  days since the last October purchase, and a dormant A- holiday-affinity interaction. The
  target window is October, so prior-October activity is a direct seasonal signal; holiday
  affinity captures seasonal shoppers who are otherwise inactive.
- The train/test split is provided and disjoint, and the target is in the future window, so
  there is no target leakage.

## 3. Models and validation

A stratified 80/20 split of the training sample gives 51,200 fit rows and 12,800 validation
rows. Because positives are only 14.6%, **PR-AUC** is the primary metric; ROC-AUC, F1,
precision, recall, log loss and Brier score are also reported. Classification thresholds are
tuned on validation F1.

| Model | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC | F1 | Precision | Recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dummy prior | 0.5000 | 0.1457 | 0.2544 | 0.1457 | 1.0000 |
| Logistic regression | 0.8717 | 0.5689 | 0.5391 | 0.4901 | 0.5989 |
| Gradient boosting (HGB) | 0.8759 | 0.5747 | 0.5473 | 0.4882 | 0.6225 |
| **Deep MLP (3-seed ensemble)** | 0.8715 | 0.5712 | 0.5465 | 0.4845 | 0.6268 |
| **Ensemble (MLP + HGB) - selected** | **0.8758** | **0.5767** | **0.5493** | 0.5096 | 0.5957 |
| Ensemble (MLP + HGB + LogReg) | 0.8756 | 0.5764 | 0.5469 | 0.4715 | 0.6509 |

The selected model is the **blend of the deep MLP and gradient boosting** (threshold 0.707).
It gives the best PR-AUC and F1 among the strong models. On the test sample it flags
**2,651 of 16,000 rows (16.6%)**. In a like-for-like HGB ablation, adding the seasonality
features improved validation PR-AUC from 0.5695 to 0.5740 and ROC-AUC from 0.8740 to 0.8756.

### Deep-learning model

A 256-128-64 MLP with batch normalisation, dropout, class-weighted binary cross-entropy,
AdamW and early stopping. Three seeds are trained and averaged, which reduces variance.
Validation PR-AUC peaks within 5-7 epochs and then overfits, so early stopping restores each
seed's best epoch. Blending with gradient boosting improves ranking stability over the MLP
alone.

### Main drivers

Permutation importance on the boosted model is dominated by behavioural recency and
frequency: sessions in the last 180 days, days since the last session, monthly average
session volume, loyalty score and tenure. Transaction spend/recency and support experience
follow. Seasonality features are used: `sess_monthly_mean` is the third most important
feature and `sess_oct_share` also enters the top ten, confirming that prior-October browsing
adds signal beyond recency alone.

### Seasonality check

Monthly revenue is strongly seasonal. Relative to the average month in the same country-year,
November averages **1.59x** and December **2.22x** (holiday average **1.90x**), while January
averages **0.64x**. Dormant customers also return in the peak: buyers whose previous order was
180+ days earlier are a larger share of buyers in Nov-Dec than in the off-season. This is why
the model includes month-aware features and why the retention planner applies a seasonal
demand adjustment instead of treating every week as average.

## 4. Segment analysis

Because the data is a sample, results are interpreted as segment estimates. Grouping by tier
shows a clear gradient: **Bronze is 63.7% of the sample but only 33.9% of expected buyers**, while
**Platinum is 8.1% of the sample but 19.4% of expected buyers**.

| Tier | Sample customers | Mean propensity | Share of expected buyers | Flag rate at 0.707 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bronze | 10,198 | 0.179 | 33.9% | 2.0% |
| Silver | 2,830 | 0.502 | 26.3% | 19.9% |
| Gold | 1,670 | 0.659 | 20.4% | 51.9% |
| Platinum | 1,302 | 0.801 | 19.4% | 78.3% |

Country is much less differentiating than tier: mean propensity is 0.32-0.34 across US, UK,
DE, FR and IN, with expected-buyer shares roughly tracking sample size (US 40.6%, UK 20.4%,
DE 19.8%, FR 9.7%, IN 9.6%).

### Customers who fall into multiple groups

Intersecting dimensions is more useful than any single cut. The table below uses **all
conditions at once** (e.g. Bronze AND active AND high session volume).

| Segment (all conditions) | Customers | Mean propensity | Share of expected buyers | Flag rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Email opt-in + high sessions | 3,132 | 0.753 | 43.8% | 65.4% |
| Bronze + email opt-in | 6,377 | 0.198 | 23.4% | 2.5% |
| Bronze + dormant | 4,594 | 0.039 | 3.3% | 0.0% |
| High loyalty + cooling | 548 | 0.603 | 6.1% | 25.4% |
| Gold/Silver + recent complaint | 221 | 0.661 | 2.7% | 46.2% |
| Bronze + active + high sessions | 197 | 0.654 | 2.4% | 34.5% |
| Open complaint (all tiers) | 70 | 0.431 | 0.6% | 27.1% |

Interpretation:

- **Email opt-in + high sessions** is about one fifth of the sample but carries **44% of
  expected buyers** - the best broad target for a consented campaign.
- **Bronze + email opt-in** is large (6,377) but low propensity (0.198); it is a reach play,
  not a high-yield one.
- **Bronze + active + high sessions** is a small niche (197) with high propensity (0.654) -
  a useful lookalike definition.
- **Bronze + dormant** (4,594) has almost no expected buyers; suppress or use a low-cost
  reactivation test only.
- **Gold/Silver + recent complaint** (221, propensity 0.661) should go to service recovery
  rather than a generic promotion.

## 5. Fairness and responsible use

- **No customer IDs or individual lookup** appear in the analysis, dashboard or exports;
  all reporting is aggregated by segment.
- **No direct identifiers** (name, email, phone) are used as features.
- **Consent:** customers with `do_not_contact` are never selected for outreach.
- **Service fairness:** customers with open complaints are excluded from promotional contact
  and routed to service recovery instead.
- **Monitoring:** selection rate is reported by country, tier and intersection segments.
  Large gaps should be reviewed before launch.
- **Predictive, not causal:** propensity ranks likely buyers; it does not estimate uplift.
  A randomised segment holdout is required before scaling incentives.
- **Human oversight:** high-value and complaint-related segments should require approval.

## 6. Agentic component (preview)

The Week 8 build includes a deterministic **policy layer** that the agent will call as a
tool. It takes propensity scores and applies:

1. consent/DNC and channel eligibility,
2. open-complaint and recent-contact suppression,
3. tier-based offer eligibility (20% / 15% voucher, free shipping, service-recovery credit),
4. weekly per-country budget caps and a maximum contact count.

Filtering happens at row level, but the output is an **aggregated segment plan** (country x
tier x offer x channel) with no customer IDs. The interactive dashboard exposes this planner,
including a policy funnel and audit trail. The next iteration wraps it as an agent tool with
an LLM reasoner for offer explanation and a human approval step.

## 7. Deliverables

| Artifact | Path |
|---|---|
| Executed checkpoint notebook | `notebooks/Week8_ShopSphere_Model_Checkpoint.ipynb` |
| Short report | `artifacts/reports/fixed/Week8_model_report.md` |
| Interactive segment explorer/tester | `archive/legacy_dashboard.py` |
| Trained models | `artifacts/models/fixed/` (preprocessor, logreg, HGB, 3 MLP seeds) |
| Metrics and predictions | `artifacts/reports/fixed/` |
| First test submission | `artifacts/outputs/submission.csv` (16,000 rows, 2,651 positives) |

## 8. Run commands

```powershell
# from the ShopSphere project root
py -m streamlit run archive/legacy_dashboard.py   # interactive segment viewer/tester
$env:PYTHONPATH="$PWD\src"; py -m shopsphere.models.train_models  # retrain + rewrite submission
```

## 9. Limitations and next steps

- **Sample, not census:** estimates describe segment tendencies; widen or reweight the
  sample before making population claims.
- **Causal vs predictive:** run a randomised segment holdout to measure incremental uplift.
- **Temporal drift:** validate on the next 30-day window and monitor calibration monthly.
- **Deep model:** try categorical embeddings and target encoding for high-cardinality fields.
- **Ensembling:** replace the fixed blend weight with a stacked meta-learner on out-of-fold
  scores.
- **Agent:** complete tool calling, explanation, guardrails and approvals.

state.output:
# ShopSphere Architecture

## Principles

- `src/` contains all runnable Python code.
- `data/raw/` receives new manual files; `data/clean/` is the validated
  prediction input; `data/processed/` is generated runtime data.
- `artifacts/` contains features, snapshots, models, reports, and exported files.
- Root entry points are thin wrappers that add `src` to `sys.path`.
- No hardcoded run dates in the active path; as-of dates are resolved from the
  data or passed through environment variables.

## Layout

```
run_all.py                 full pipeline entry point
app.py                     Streamlit entry point
planner.py                 weekly planner entry point
src/shopsphere/
  common.py                paths, feature lists, shared helpers
  data/
    asof_time.py           as-of resolution and window bounds
    asof_features.py       point-in-time feature builder
    build_features.py      fixed official feature builder
    validate_clean.py      model-input validation and data-quality report
  features/
    prep_contacts.py       historical/current contact preparation
    build_analytics.py     W6/W10 analytics tables
  models/
    mlp_model.py           PyTorch MLP
    scoring.py             fixed and rolling scorers
    train_models.py        fixed W1 model
    snapshot_builder.py    monthly as-of snapshots
    train_rolling.py       rolling W1 train/backtest/live scoring
    train_offer.py         offer purchase and redemption models
    score_offers.py        customer x offer x channel scoring
  pipelines/
    run_all.py             end-to-end orchestration
    planner.py             weekly budgeted recommendation plan
  app/
    app.py                 Streamlit dashboard
    approvals.py           W9 approval workflow and SQLite audit log
data/raw/             new manual files awaiting validation and cleaning
data/clean/                cleaned source CSVs; sole prediction input
data/processed/            contacts, scores, analytics CSVs, approvals.sqlite
artifacts/features/        fixed feature pickles and metadata
artifacts/snapshots/       rolling snapshots and manifest
artifacts/models/          fixed/, rolling/, offer/
artifacts/reports/         fixed/, rolling/, offer/, analytics/, plans/, logs/
artifacts/outputs/         plans, submissions, approved exports
```

## Data flow

New data is added manually to `data/raw/`, cleaned, and promoted into
`data/clean/`; the latest transaction date there is the live as-of. Prediction
code reads only from `data/clean/`. If an agentic cleaning step is added later,
it should work in `data/raw/` and promote only validated, cleaned files
into `data/clean/`.

1. `validate_clean.py` checks files, keys, references, dates and ranges, then
   writes `artifacts/reports/data_quality.json`.
2. `snapshot_builder.py` builds monthly as-of snapshots from clean data.
3. `train_rolling.py` trains MLP, HGB, and logistic regression, tunes the
   ensemble threshold on the validation month, refits, and writes live scores.
4. `prep_contacts.py` joins live scores to current customers and historical
   contact features.
5. `train_offer.py` trains purchase/redemption models on a dynamic time split.
6. `score_offers.py` creates customer x offer x channel candidates.
7. `build_analytics.py` writes W6/W10 tables.
8. `planner.py` and `app.py` consume processed data and artifacts.

## Artifact ownership

| Path | Producer |
| --- | --- |
| `data/processed/*.pkl`, `*.parquet`, `*.csv` | prep/scoring/analytics |
| `data/processed/approvals.sqlite` | approvals |
| `artifacts/features/` | build_features |
| `artifacts/snapshots/` | snapshot_builder |
| `artifacts/models/fixed/` | train_models |
| `artifacts/models/rolling/` | train_rolling |
| `artifacts/models/offer/` | train_offer |
| `artifacts/reports/fixed/` | train_models |
| `artifacts/reports/rolling/` | train_rolling |
| `artifacts/reports/offer/` | train_offer, score_offers |
| `artifacts/reports/analytics/` | build_analytics |
| `artifacts/reports/data_quality.json` | validate_clean |
| `artifacts/reports/plans/` | planner |
| `artifacts/outputs/` | planner, approvals, train_models |

def tab_campaigns() -> None:
    st.subheader("Campaign effectiveness and incrementality")
    st.caption(
        "Attribution metrics are platform-attributed. The DiD view is a quasi-experimental "
        "region comparison and should not be read as a randomised causal estimate."
    )
    monthly = analytics("analytics_campaign_type.csv")
    monthly["month"] = pd.to_datetime(monthly["month"])
    types = sorted(monthly["campaign_type"].dropna().unique())
    selected = st.multiselect("Campaign types", types, default=types)
    m = monthly[monthly["campaign_type"].isin(selected)].copy()
    if m.empty:
        st.warning("No campaign rows.")
        return

    totals = m.groupby("campaign_type").agg(
        campaigns=("campaigns", "sum"), spend=("spend", "sum"),
        revenue=("attributed_revenue", "sum"), orders=("attributed_orders", "sum"),
        clicks=("clicks", "sum"), impressions=("impressions", "sum"),
    ).reset_index()
    totals["roas"] = totals["revenue"] / totals["spend"].replace(0, float("nan"))
    totals["cpa"] = totals["spend"] / totals["orders"].replace(0, float("nan"))
    totals["ctr"] = totals["clicks"] / totals["impressions"].replace(0, float("nan"))
    totals = totals.sort_values("roas", ascending=False)

    c1, c2 = st.columns([1, 1])
    with c1:
        bar = alt.Chart(totals).mark_bar().encode(
            x=alt.X("campaign_type:N", sort="-y", title=None),
            y=alt.Y("roas:Q", title="Attributed ROAS"),
            color=alt.Color("campaign_type:N", legend=None),
            tooltip=["campaign_type:N", alt.Tooltip("roas:Q", format=".2f"),
                     alt.Tooltip("spend:Q", format="$,.0f")],
        ).properties(height=300)
        st.altair_chart(bar, width="stretch")
    with c2:
        show = totals[["campaign_type", "spend", "revenue", "orders", "roas", "cpa", "ctr"]].copy()
        show.columns = ["Type", "Spend", "Revenue", "Orders", "ROAS", "CPA", "CTR"]
        show["Spend"] = show["Spend"].map(fmt_money)
        show["Revenue"] = show["Revenue"].map(fmt_money)
        show["ROAS"] = show["ROAS"].map(lambda x: f"{x:.2f}")
        show["CPA"] = show["CPA"].map(fmt_money)
        show["CTR"] = show["CTR"].map(fmt_pct)
        show_table(show)

    trend = alt.Chart(m).mark_line(point=False).encode(
        x=alt.X("month:T", title=None),
        y=alt.Y("roas:Q", title="Monthly ROAS"),
        color=alt.Color("campaign_type:N", title="Type"),
        tooltip=["month:T", "campaign_type:N", alt.Tooltip("roas:Q", format=".2f")],
    ).properties(height=280)
    st.altair_chart(trend, width="stretch")

    st.divider()
    st.markdown("**Retention offer lift vs reminder-only (`OFF-NONE`)**")
    lift_path = os.path.join(OUT_DATA, "analytics_offer_lift.csv")
    if os.path.exists(lift_path):
        lift = load_csv(lift_path)
        base = alt.Chart(lift)
        bars = base.mark_bar(color="#2b8a9e").encode(
            x=alt.X("offer_code:N", sort="-y", title=None),
            y=alt.Y("adjusted_lift:Q", title="Adjusted purchase-rate lift"),
            tooltip=["offer_code:N", alt.Tooltip("adjusted_lift:Q", format=".3f"),
                     alt.Tooltip("contacts:Q", format=",.0f")],
        )
        rules = base.mark_rule(color="#333").encode(
            x="offer_code:N", y="lift_ci_low:Q", y2="lift_ci_high:Q",
        )
        st.altair_chart(bars + rules, width="stretch")
        show = lift.copy()
        show.columns = [
            "Offer", "Contacts", "Observed rate", "Baseline rate", "Adjusted lift",
            "CI low", "CI high", "Incremental purchases", "Redemption rate",
            "None rate",
        ]
        for col in ["Observed rate", "Baseline rate", "Adjusted lift", "CI low",
                    "CI high", "Redemption rate", "None rate"]:
            show[col] = show[col].map(lambda x: f"{x:.2%}")
        show["Incremental purchases"] = show["Incremental purchases"].map(lambda x: f"{x:,.1f}")
        show_table(show)
        st.caption(
            "Lift is direct-standardised to the offer group's tier × country × channel mix. "
            "Intervals crossing zero mean the offer effect is not distinguishable from no effect."
        )
    else:
        st.info("Run build_analytics.py to generate offer lift.")

    st.divider()
    st.markdown("**Regional campaign differences-in-differences**")
    did_path = os.path.join(OUT_DATA, "analytics_campaign_did.csv")
    if os.path.exists(did_path):
        did = load_csv(did_path)
        c1, c2 = st.columns(2)
        dcountry = c1.multiselect("DiD countries", sorted(did["country"].dropna().unique()),
                                  default=sorted(did["country"].dropna().unique()))
        dtype = c2.multiselect("DiD types", sorted(did["campaign_type"].dropna().unique()),
                               default=sorted(did["campaign_type"].dropna().unique()))
        view = did[did["country"].isin(dcountry) & did["campaign_type"].isin(dtype)].copy()
        view = view.sort_values("relative_lift", ascending=False)
        view = view[[
            "campaign_id", "campaign_type", "country", "target_region", "start_date",
            "end_date", "post_days", "n_control_regions", "did_daily_revenue",
            "relative_lift", "target_pre_orders", "target_post_orders",
        ]].copy()
        view.columns = [
            "Campaign", "Type", "Country", "Target region", "Start", "End", "Days",
            "Controls", "DiD daily revenue", "Relative lift", "Target pre orders",
            "Target post orders",
        ]
        view["DiD daily revenue"] = view["DiD daily revenue"].map(fmt_money)
        view["Relative lift"] = view["Relative lift"].map(fmt_pct)
        show_table(view.head(100))

def tab_recommendations() -> None:
    st.subheader("W3 weekly retention plan")
    st.caption(
        "Plans use the offer-response model and are constrained by country budget, consent, "
        "service-recovery routing, and a contact cooldown. Costs are redemption-weighted "
        "expected incentive spend."
    )
    budget = read_budget()
    weeks = sorted(budget["week_start"].dt.date.unique())
    countries = sorted(budget["country"].unique())
    c1, c2, c3, c4 = st.columns(4)
    week = c1.selectbox("Week", weeks)
    country = c2.selectbox("Country", countries)
    objective = c3.selectbox(
        "Objective", list(planner.OBJECTIVES.keys()),
        format_func=lambda x: planner.OBJECTIVES[x],
        index=0,
    )
    budget_default = planner.budget_for(pd.Timestamp(week), country)
    budget_usd = c4.number_input("Budget cap (USD)", min_value=0.0, value=float(budget_default),
                                 step=500.0)

    c1, c2, c3, c4 = st.columns(4)
    min_uplift = c1.slider("Minimum uplift", 0.0, 0.20, 0.0, 0.005, format="%.3f")
    min_net = c2.number_input("Minimum expected net per contact", value=0.0, step=1.0)
    cooldown = c3.slider("Contact cooldown (days)", 0, 60, 14, 1)
    max_contacts = c4.number_input("Max contacts (0 = no cap)", min_value=0, value=0, step=1000)

    plan_key = (
        str(week), country, objective, round(float(budget_usd), 2),
        round(float(min_uplift), 4), round(float(min_net), 2),
        int(cooldown), int(max_contacts),
    )
    if st.button("Build plan", type="primary"):
        with st.spinner("Scoring and allocating ..."):
            plan, summary = planner.build_plan(
                week, country, budget_usd, objective, min_uplift,
                min_net_value=min_net,
                max_contacts=int(max_contacts) if max_contacts else None,
                cooldown_days=cooldown,
                scores=load_scores(),
            )
        st.session_state["plan"] = plan
        st.session_state["plan_summary"] = summary
        st.session_state["plan_key"] = plan_key

    plan = st.session_state.get("plan")
    summary = st.session_state.get("plan_summary")
    if plan is None or summary is None:
        st.info("Choose the week, country and guardrails, then build a plan.")
        return
    if st.session_state.get("plan_key") != plan_key:
        st.warning("Settings changed since this plan was built. Build a new plan to continue.")
        return
    st.caption(
        f"Plan for {summary['week_start']} · {summary['country']} · "
        f"{summary['objective_label']} · Budget {fmt_money(summary['budget_usd'])}"
    )
    if summary.get("score_as_of"):
        st.caption(
            f"W1 live snapshot {summary['score_as_of']} · target window "
            f"{summary.get('score_window_start')} to {summary.get('score_window_end')} · "
            f"model {summary.get('score_model') or 'rolling ensemble'}"
        )
    seasonal_note = summary.get("seasonal_note")
    if seasonal_note:
        st.info(f"Seasonality adjustment: {seasonal_note}")
    if plan.empty:
        st.warning(
            "No recommendations meet the current guardrails. Lower the minimum net value, "
            "reduce the cooldown, or choose another objective."
        )
        return

    k1, k2, k3, k4, k5 = st.columns(5)
    k1.metric("Contacts", f"{summary['planned_contacts']:,}")
    k2.metric("Expected spend", fmt_money(summary["planned_spend"]))
    k3.metric("Incremental revenue", fmt_money(summary["expected_incremental_revenue"]))
    k4.metric("Expected net margin", fmt_money(summary["expected_net_value"]))
    k5.metric("Expected ROI", f"{summary['expected_roi']:.2f}" if summary["expected_roi"] is not None else "n/a")

    c1, c2 = st.columns(2)
    with c1:
        offer_mix = pd.DataFrame(
            {"offer": list(summary["offer_mix"].keys()),
             "contacts": list(summary["offer_mix"].values())}
        )
        st.altair_chart(
            alt.Chart(offer_mix).mark_bar().encode(
                x=alt.X("contacts:Q", title="Contacts"),
                y=alt.Y("offer:N", sort="-x", title=None),
                tooltip=["offer:N", "contacts:Q"],
            ).properties(height=220),
            width="stretch",
        )
    with c2:
        channel_mix = pd.DataFrame(
            {"channel": list(summary["channel_mix"].keys()),
             "contacts": list(summary["channel_mix"].values())}
        )
        st.altair_chart(
            alt.Chart(channel_mix).mark_bar().encode(
                x=alt.X("contacts:Q", title="Contacts"),
                y=alt.Y("channel:N", sort="-x", title=None),
                color=alt.Color("channel:N", legend=None),
                tooltip=["channel:N", "contacts:Q"],
            ).properties(height=220),
            width="stretch",
        )

    display_cols = [
        "priority_rank", "sample_ref", "cust_country", "cust_tier", "channel", "offer_code",
        "purchase_probability", "baseline_probability", "uplift", "redemption_probability",
        "offer_cost", "expected_incremental_revenue", "expected_net_value", "roi",
        "w1_probability", "priority_score",
    ]
    show = plan[[c for c in display_cols if c in plan.columns]].copy()
    show.columns = [
        "Rank", "Sample ref", "Country", "Tier", "Channel", "Offer",
        "Purchase prob.", "Baseline prob.", "Uplift", "Redemption prob.",
        "Expected cost", "Incremental revenue", "Expected net", "ROI",
        "W1 prob.", "Priority score",
    ][:len(show.columns)]
    for col in ["Purchase prob.", "Baseline prob.", "Uplift", "Redemption prob.", "W1 prob."]:
        if col in show.columns:
            show[col] = show[col].map(fmt_pct)
    for col in ["Expected cost", "Incremental revenue", "Expected net", "Priority score"]:
        if col in show.columns:
            show[col] = show[col].map(fmt_money)
    if "ROI" in show.columns:
        show["ROI"] = show["ROI"].map(lambda x: f"{x:.2f}" if pd.notna(x) else "n/a")
    show_table(show.head(500))
    st.caption(f"Showing up to 500 of {len(plan):,} recommendations. The CSV contains all rows.")

    csv = plan.to_csv(index=False).encode("utf-8")
    c1, c2, c3 = st.columns([1, 1, 2])
    c1.download_button(
        "Download plan CSV", csv,
        file_name=f"plan_{week}_{country}.csv", mime="text/csv",
        width="stretch",
    )
    with c2:
        prepared_by = st.text_input("Prepared by", value="", key="prepared_by")
    with c3:
        st.write("")
        st.write("")
        created_ref = (
            st.session_state.get("batch_ref")
            if st.session_state.get("batch_key") == plan_key else None
        )
        if created_ref:
            st.info(f"Approval batch {created_ref} already created for this plan.")
        elif st.button("Create approval batch", width="stretch"):
            try:
                ref = approvals.create_batch(plan, summary, prepared_by or "planner")
                st.session_state["batch_key"] = plan_key
                st.session_state["batch_ref"] = ref
                st.success(f"Created {ref}. Open the Approvals tab to review it.")
            except Exception as exc:
                st.error(str(exc))

# ShopSphere Global: Retention and Re-engagement Offer Policy

Version 3.2. Owner: CRM and Retention team. Effective 1 July 2024.

## 1. Purpose
This policy sets out who may receive a retention or re-engagement offer, which offers may be used, and the limits that apply. It applies to every outbound retention contact: email, SMS, app push and WhatsApp.

## 2. Who must never be contacted
1. Customers with `do_not_contact = Y` in the customer preference centre.
2. Email offers: customers with `email_opt_in = N`. SMS offers: customers with `sms_opt_in = N`.
3. Customers with an **open High-priority support ticket** (lost parcel or payment issue). These customers must be handled by Customer Service first. A promotional message sent while their complaint is open is treated as a service failure.
4. Customers contacted with any retention offer in the last **30 days**. Offers with `counts_toward_monthly_limit = 0` in the offer catalogue are exempt.

## 3. Offer eligibility by tier
Offer codes and values are listed in `offer_catalogue.csv`.

| Tier | Offers allowed | Maximum voucher |
|---|---|---|
| Bronze | OFF-NONE, OFF-FS, OFF-V10 | 10% |
| Silver | Bronze offers plus OFF-V15 | 15% |
| Gold | Silver offers plus OFF-PTS2 | 15% |
| Platinum | All offers including OFF-V20 | 20% |

OFF-SRC (service-recovery credit) may be used for any tier, but only where the customer had a confirmed service failure in the last 60 days: a late or lost delivery, or a damaged or wrong item.

## 4. Product and stock rules
1. Vouchers must not be promoted on products marked `is_promotable = No` (margin below 18%).
2. Do not feature a product in a personalised message if `stock_on_hand = 0`, or if `stock_on_hand < 50` and the next restock is more than 14 days away.

## 5. Budget
1. Each country has a weekly retention budget (`retention_budget_2024Q4.csv`). The cost of an offer is the expected redemption cost:
   - Vouchers: voucher % A- customer's average order value A- expected redemption rate. The redemption rate must be estimated from `retention_contact_history.csv`; if it cannot be estimated for a segment, use 10%.
   - Shipping: $6.00 A- redemption rate.
   - Points: $3.00 A- redemption rate.
   - Service-recovery credit: $10.00. It is always counted at full cost.
2. Unused budget does not carry over to the next week.
3. Any single offer with an expected cost above $25 needs approval from the CRM Manager.

## 6. Contact rules
1. Use the customer's `preferred_channel` and `preferred_language` where consent allows.
2. No more than 2 marketing messages of any kind per customer per week, including campaign emails.
3. Quiet period: no SMS or WhatsApp between 9 pm and 8 am, customer local time.
4. Every message must include an unsubscribe option and must not imply urgency that is not true ("last chance" only when it really is).

## 7. Approval and audit
Every retention list must be approved by a CRM Executive before it is sent. Lists generated by automated tools must record, for each customer, the reason they were selected and the offer chosen.
# ShopSphere Global: ShopSphere Rewards Loyalty Programme

## 1. Tiers
A customer's tier is based on what they spent in the last 12 months and is recalculated on the first day of each month.

| Tier | 12-month spend | Benefits |
|---|---|---|
| Bronze | under $120 | 1 point per $1 |
| Silver | $120 to $399 | 1.25 points per $1, birthday voucher |
| Gold | $400 to $899 | 1.5 points per $1, free express shipping twice a year |
| Platinum | $900 and above | 2 points per $1, free express shipping, priority support |

## 2. Points
100 points = $1 off. Points expire 12 months after they are earned.

## 3. Loyalty score
`loyalty_score` (0�?"1) is an internal engagement index calculated by the CRM system. It is not shown to customers, and it is not the same thing as tier.

# ShopSphere Global: Customer Service Standards and SLA

Version 1.9. Owner: Customer Service.

## 1. Response and resolution targets
| Priority | Typical categories | First response | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| High | Lost parcel, Payment issue | 4 hours | 24 hours |
| Medium | Late delivery, Damaged or wrong item, Refund status | 12 hours | 72 hours |
| Low | Account access, Product question, Promo code, Cancel order | 24 hours | 5 days |

## 2. Escalation
1. A ticket that misses its resolution target is escalated to a Team Lead.
2. A customer with 2 or more tickets in 30 days is flagged as "at risk". The agent handling the ticket must check the customer's history before replying.
3. Platinum customers with any open High-priority ticket are escalated straight away.

## 3. Customer satisfaction (CSAT)
CSAT surveys are sent when a ticket is closed (1 = very dissatisfied, 5 = very satisfied). About half of customers respond. The team target is an average CSAT of 4.0 or above.

## 4. Coordination with Marketing
Customer Service must be able to see whether a customer received a marketing or retention offer in the last 14 days. Marketing must not send promotions to customers with an open High-priority ticket (see the Retention Offer Policy, section 2).
# ShopSphere Global: Shipping, Delivery and Returns Policy

Version 2.4. Owner: Operations.

## 1. Shipping options
| Option | Promised delivery | Fee |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | 6 business days after dispatch | Free over $50, otherwise $4.99 |
| Express | 3 business days after dispatch | $9.99 |
| Overnight | Next business day after dispatch | $19.99 |

Orders are dispatched the day after payment. During the peak season (1 November to 31 December), promised dates may be extended by up to 3 days. Customers are told this at checkout.

## 2. Late deliveries
1. A delivery is **late** if it arrives after the promised date.
2. Late by 1�?"2 days: apologise and update tracking. No compensation is required.
3. Late by 3 or more days: refund the shipping fee on request (Express and Overnight), or offer OFF-SRC if the customer complains.
4. Two or more late deliveries in 60 days: the customer qualifies for OFF-SRC without having to complain.

## 3. Lost parcels
A parcel is treated as lost if tracking has not updated for 7 days, or if the carrier confirms loss. The customer is offered a full refund or a free replacement at their choice, and an OFF-SRC credit.

## 4. Returns and refunds
1. Items can be returned within 30 days of delivery. Groceries and opened beauty products cannot be returned.
2. Refunds are processed within 5 business days of receiving the return and reach the customer's account within 10 business days.
3. Damaged or wrong items: free return label, plus a replacement or refund. No questions asked within 7 days of delivery.

## 5. Carriers
SwiftPost, ParcelNow (US, UK, India), GlobalExpress (all markets), RoyalLine (UK), DeutschLog (Germany), ColisFast (France), BharatShip (India). Carrier performance is reviewed every quarter by Operations.

This reveals significant policy inconsistencies:
- Retention policy: never contact customers with open **High-priority** ticket (lost parcel or payment issue), not all open tickets. Current `service_ok` uses `sup_recent_complaint` (recent 90d complaint categories) AND `sup_open_n > 0`; this may exclude/allow incorrectly. It doesn't specifically filter High-priority open ticket. It also allows OFF-SRC for recent complaint + open. Need align.
- Contact frequency: no retention offer in last 30 days, offers with counts_monthly=0 exempt. Current planner uses 14-day cooldown, not 30 days. Major mismatch.
- Tier offers: OFF-FS is allowed for all tiers? Table says Bronze allows OFF-FS, OFF-V10; Silver plus V15; Gold plus PTS2; Platinum all incl V20. `offer_catalogue` eligible_tiers: OFF-FS All, V10 All, V15 Silver/Gold/Platinum, V20 Platinum, PTS2 Gold/Platinum, SRC All. That aligns mostly, except OFF-FS All includes all tiers, okay (Bronze allowed). But policy table says Bronze allowed OFF-FS, V10; Silver Bronze + V15; Gold Silver + PTS2; Platinum all. `offer_catalogue` V15 eligible Silver,Gold,Platinum; V20 Platinum; PTS2 Gold,Platinum; good.
- Product stock rule: current `requires_promotable` only checks customer has any promotable item, not `stock_on_hand=0` or low stock/restock >14 days. Not enforced. `products.stock_on_hand` not used. Major.
- Budget: offer cost expected redemption; current `offer_cost = face_value * redemption_probability`, yes. But for service-recovery credit, policy says always full cost; current `offer_face_value` for OFF-SRC? `offer_cost_series` likely uses value * redemption? Let's inspect. If OFF-SRC face value 10 and `offer_cost = face_value * redemption_probability`, it's not full cost. Misaligned. Also if redemption rate can't be estimated use 10%; current model predicts. Fine.
- Single offer expected cost > $25 needs CRM Manager approval. Current approval is batch-level, not per-offer cost threshold; no rule.
- Contact rules: preferred channel/language; no more than 2 messages/week; quiet period; unsubscribe. Current planner uses `contact_channel_is_preferred` feature but doesn't filter to preferred channel. It includes all channels for each customer; `channel_ok` only consent. Could select non-preferred channels. It doesn't enforce 2/week or quiet period. It doesn't include unsubscribe text (simulated, no messages). For prototype, maybe okay but W4.
- Approval: every retention list approved by CRM Executive; current approvals requires actor/reason but no role check. Good enough.
- W3 budget: `budget_for` uses weekly budget, good. But "unused budget doesn't carry over" not relevant.
- W10 campaign effectiveness: app uses platform attribution and DiD. Good, but caveat.
- W6: dashboard includes sales, traffic, campaign, delivery, customer activity. Need check if traffic/customer activity? The overview metrics: revenue, orders, AOV, conversion, ROAS, late delivery. Charts. Seasonality. Does it show "customer activity"? Maybe propensity tab. W6 asks trends in sales, traffic, campaign performance, delivery performance and customer activity, by country and over time. Overview has revenue/orders/sessions/conversion (traffic), campaign ROAS, late delivery. Customer activity maybe sessions. Seasonality. Could be sufficient. But no explicit "customer activity" metric like active customers/reactivated? Analytics has `analytics_customer_activity.csv` maybe. Need inspect app overview rest lines 134-160.

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import sqlite3
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone

import pandas as pd

from shopsphere.common import DB_PATH, OUT_OUTPUTS, ensure_dirs

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS batches (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    batch_ref TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by TEXT NOT NULL,
    week_start TEXT NOT NULL,
    country TEXT NOT NULL,
    objective TEXT NOT NULL,
    budget_usd REAL,
    planned_contacts INTEGER NOT NULL,
    planned_spend REAL,
    expected_incremental_revenue REAL,
    expected_net_value REAL,
    expected_roi REAL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Pending',
    decided_by TEXT,
    decided_at TEXT,
    decision_reason TEXT,
    summary_json TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS recommendations (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    batch_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    sample_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
    cust_country TEXT,
    cust_tier TEXT,
    channel TEXT,
    offer_code TEXT,
    offer_type TEXT,
    purchase_probability REAL,
    baseline_probability REAL,
    uplift REAL,
    redemption_probability REAL,
    expected_order_value REAL,
    offer_cost REAL,
    expected_incremental_revenue REAL,
    expected_net_value REAL,
    roi REAL,
    w1_probability REAL,
    priority_rank INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (batch_id) REFERENCES batches(id)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_log (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    batch_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    action TEXT NOT NULL,
    actor TEXT NOT NULL,
    reason TEXT,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (batch_id) REFERENCES batches(id)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_recommendations_batch ON recommendations(batch_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_audit_batch ON audit_log(batch_id);
"""


def connect() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    ensure_dirs()
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
    return conn


def now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat()


def py(value):
    if pd.isna(value):
        return None
    if hasattr(value, "item"):
        return value.item()
    return value


def create_batch(plan: pd.DataFrame, summary: dict, created_by: str = "system") -> str:
    if plan is None or len(plan) == 0:
        raise ValueError("Cannot create an empty approval batch")
    if not str(created_by).strip():
        raise ValueError("created_by is required")
    batch_ref = (
        f"BATCH-{summary['week_start']}-{summary['country']}-"
        f"{datetime.now().strftime('%H%M%S')}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:4].upper()}"
    )
    conn = connect()
    try:
        cur = conn.cursor()
        cur.execute(
            """INSERT INTO batches (
                batch_ref, created_at, created_by, week_start, country, objective,
                budget_usd, planned_contacts, planned_spend, expected_incremental_revenue,
                expected_net_value, expected_roi, status, summary_json
            ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'Pending', ?)""",
            (
                batch_ref, now(), created_by, summary["week_start"], summary["country"],
                summary["objective"], py(summary.get("budget_usd")),
                int(summary["planned_contacts"]), py(summary.get("planned_spend")),
                py(summary.get("expected_incremental_revenue")),
                py(summary.get("expected_net_value")), py(summary.get("expected_roi")),
                json.dumps(summary, default=str),
            ),
        )
        batch_id = int(cur.lastrowid)
        rec_cols = [
            "sample_ref", "cust_country", "cust_tier", "channel", "offer_code",
            "offer_type", "purchase_probability", "baseline_probability", "uplift",
            "redemption_probability", "expected_order_value", "offer_cost",
            "expected_incremental_revenue", "expected_net_value", "roi",
            "w1_probability", "priority_rank",
        ]
        rows = []
        for _, r in plan.iterrows():
            rows.append(tuple([batch_id] + [py(r.get(c)) for c in rec_cols]))
        placeholders = ", ".join(["?"] * (len(rec_cols) + 1))
        cur.executemany(
            f"INSERT INTO recommendations (batch_id, {', '.join(rec_cols)}) "
            f"VALUES ({placeholders})", rows,
        )
        cur.execute(
            "INSERT INTO audit_log (batch_id, action, actor, reason, created_at) "
            "VALUES (?, 'created', ?, ?, ?)",
            (batch_id, created_by, f"Created batch with {len(plan)} recommendations", now()),
        )
        conn.commit()
        return batch_ref
    finally:
        conn.close()


def list_batches() -> pd.DataFrame:
    conn = connect()
    try:
        return pd.read_sql_query(
            "SELECT * FROM batches ORDER BY id DESC", conn,
        )
